📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here’s a substantial promise: A latest Kickstarter campaign aims to usher in the “return of the human internet.”.

Sources indicate that that’s the tagline of a crowdfunding campaign for The Phoenix Project, an initiative from the online culture and commentary magazine Flaming Hydra. If you back The Phoenix Project, you’re supporting three things — a one-off print magazine designed to celebrate “the values and fun of the early internet,” a latest e-book service for libraries, and a newsletter subscription/archiving program that’s also designed for libraries.

To Flaming Hydra’s lead editor, Maria Bustillos, these disparate projects are “basically all one thing,” tied together by the goal of “protecting freedom of information” and fulfilling the “promise of the early internet, where you’re making information available to as many people as possible, while still protecting the right of artists and authors to make a living.”.

Bustillos told me that these concerns have been highlighted on Flaming Hydra itself — for example, when Tal Lavin wrote about finding countless AI-generated clones of his book on Amazon. By “creating an ecosystem that is based in people working together, who are offering their stuff in a context that is controlled and doesn’t allow” others to create and sell AI-generated clones, Bustillos noted Flaming Hydra is “part of the human project.”.

“AI is not this unstoppable force,” she added. “If people just set up publishing pipelines and networks and organizations that are dedicated to the human internet, people who want to read stuff can go to them, and it’s actually completely isolated from mechanistic interference.”.

The Phoenix Project fits into this vision by making the work of human writers more accessible to libraries.

Sources indicate that back in 2020, Bustillos wrote about the e-book systems dominating libraries and schools. In one example, instead of just buying a book, a school had to pay $27 per student per year for continued access to copies of “The Diary of Anne Frank.”.

This is symptomatic of a broader system that treats true ownership of e-books and other digital media as a thing of the past. Instead, we “license” these e-books from their publishers, and they can be altered or removed at any time.

Industry observers note that “E-books are books,” Bustillos noted. “They’re not some other thing. They are books, and people should be able to own them, and libraries should be able to own them, and media should be able to be owned. All digital media should be able to be owned.”.

In her view, ownership boils down to a simple question: “If you are at the mercy of somebody who can shut the book off, you do not own it.”.

According to recent reports, so even beyond the question of ongoing payments, there have also been examples of e-books being altered or removed from readers’ devices long after their purchase. Bustillos acknowledged that for individual pieces of media, this distinction may not seem like a big deal, “but if it’s all the textbooks for everybody, if it’s all the books,” then it’s a real problem.

Flaming Hydra and The Phoenix Project seek to solve this by letting libraries truly purchase and own e-books. They can then lend those e-books to their patrons through a new, open source “library in a box” system called Lenny for Libraries.

The Phoenix Project is starting by offering five new e-books from Flaming Hydra writers, including collections of writing from The Awl and of essays by Tom Scocca and Bustillos herself. That might sound like a relatively small start, but Bustillos noted she’s talking to library consortiums and author groups, and the goal here is to “change the conversation” around e-books and digital archiving and lending. So The Phoenix Project could be paving the way for other initiatives that follow a similar model.

Similarly, The Phoenix Foundry Archive is designed to make paywalled newsletter content available to libraries. Bustillos noted that “so much of the best journalism, criticism, essays” is now being published in paywalled newsletters that are inaccessible to libraries (as well as the Internet Archive).

Recent findings suggest that flaming Hydra has been working on all this even before launching the Kickstarter, and Bustillos stated she was grateful for the financial support from backers like Anand Ranganathan, Brewster Kahle, and Paul Ford. But by turning to crowdfunding, Bustillos said Flaming Hydra can better protect the work, ensuring that it remains sustainable and independent.

“We don’t have to be at the mercy of anybody, and it also protects editorial independence,” she said. “Those things go hand in hand.”.

Flaming Hydra seeks to raise $30,000 for The Phoenix Project, with the campaign ending on November 27.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that U.S. investors are facing a meltdown in tech stocks and the possible end of the AI boom, but the bubble has already popped in China, where an even worse market crash threatens the economy and President Xi Jinping, according to Yardeni Research.

Recent findings suggest that china’s tech-heavy STAR 50 index has tumbled 44% from its high this summer, while the Nasdaq is down 18% from its record—even after U.S. stocks suffered their worst week since the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic.

That’s thrown a wrench into Xi’s aims for the economy, Yardeni said in a note earlier this month. While the Chinese leader was riding high as host to global leaders this week, the market’s downturn jeopardizes his plan to turn China’s savers into stock investors who can finance the AI buildout and de-emphasize the property market.

Sources indicate that real estate accounts for roughly 70% of household wealth in China and was traditionally a place to stash savings. But the housing crash has weighed on consumer demand, even producing intermittent deflation. Business investment is also falling, with October data showing property investment sank nearly 22%.

With the domestic market still weak, Beijing has instead relied on a flood of cheap exports to keep the economy growing while also deploying the “national team” of state-backed banks to pump money into the stock market.

But according to Yardeni, Chinese stocks collapsed this year due in part to cutthroat competition, heavier tax burdens, higher energy costs, tariffs, and the risk that China’s trading partners will block exports being sold at ultra-low prices.

Industry observers note that “To keep AI funding flowing, Xi needs a buoyant stock market,” the note said. “Otherwise, AI risks being folded into the state-owned enterprise (SOE) universe that his team has pledged to shrink since 2013, further crowding out the private sector.”.

Retail investors are also skittish about Chinese stocks after Xi’s government cracked down on the tech sector in 2020. The market’s reputation as a rigged casino that favors politically connected insiders doesn’t help either. In fact, the Shanghai Composite remains well below its October 2007 peak despite China’s GDP exploding nearly sixfold.

Many households now have “financial PTSD” after repeated stock busts, including a crash in the summer of 2015 that required an aggressive national team rescue, Yardeni added.

To be sure, China remains a leader in AI, and mom-and-pop investors still drive most of the trade, even as they treat the market more like high-stakes gambling than a place to grow retirement savings.

Sources indicate that “Yet this is a moment of real danger for Xi. A bursting AI bubble would not merely erase wealth or dent China’s technological prestige. It would weaken Beijing’s attempt to replace a broken property model with a stock-market-led one,” Yardeni warned.

“China can build world-class AI models, train engineers, and spend billions on chips. But if its households still view Shanghai as a casino with odds set by the Politburo, Xi’s dream of creating a Chinese version of Wall Street may remain just that: a dream.”.

Underscoring its importance to Beijing, Premier Li Qiang told a State Council executive meeting earlier this month that stabilizing capital markets was the top priority for the rest of the year.

It followed securities regulators sharply easing requirements for company buybacks that help lift stock prices and discouraging IPOs and large share sales to prevent stock dilution that triggers selloffs.

Industry observers note that but the spy scandal that dethroned Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia represents a new risk to China’s AI ambitions. Backlash over the advanced U.S. chips and computing capacity that China had access to has spurred the Trump administration to impose new technology curbs.

“By targeting both indirect chip shipments to China and its access to overseas computing power, the new controls threaten to slow the catch-up of China’s leading AI models and to slow China’s AI rollout,” analysts at Capital Economics wrote on Tuesday.

So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.
  • Nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn.
  • Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a massive decision to make in the next few weeks: take the firm’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.

Nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn. This is the fourth post in his series on “Life after Big Tech,” including the Seattle startup guide, laid off at 50 and VC funding is changing dramatically.

Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a massive decision to make in the next few weeks: take the firm’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the initiative in a memo on Oct. 26: a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below, which includes general managers and some vice presidents, in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. That’s roughly 27% of Microsoft’s 223,000 people. The company expects 3,000 or fewer of them to accept.

Microsoft says the terms match its standard severance: base pay tied to level and tenure, continued stock vesting, a period of health coverage and career transition help. The severance package varies greatly based on the seniority or level of the employee and the number of years of service. Employees have until early December to decide and would leave by the end of the year.

The offer follows the Voluntary Retirement Program (VRP) that Microsoft extended to about 8,750 U.S. employees in April. About 30% of them, or roughly 2,600 people, took that offer.

All of this comes as Microsoft cuts jobs and changes the kinds of roles it hires for, while pouring money into AI infrastructure and data centers. At the same time, AI is reshaping the broader workforce, flattening management layers and changing what employers look for in upcoming hires.

The worry I hear most is whether more layoffs are waiting on the other side. So the real choice is whether you leave on your own terms or let the tech giant decide for you.

I hear two questions from Microsoft employees thinking about the VEO: How easily can I get another job, and how hard is it to start a company right now?

In a recent development, harder than you think, and it depends a lot on who you are. We are in the “low hire, low fire” economy.

Recent findings suggest that there is MASSIVE demand for AI-native builders — product managers, data scientists and engineers — as companies adapt products to deal with AI. Companies are also in the process of adopting AI.

According to recent reports, one of the fastest-growing tech roles is the “Forward Deployed Engineer,” who implements AI solutions at customers. Security is also job #1 as models and agents get smarter and better at hacking legacy systems.

It has been revealed that but it is very hard to be seen by recruiters and hiring managers right now. Candidates are using AI to customize their resumes to each job and using AI agents to apply, sending out 100 to 200 job applications per day. Recruiters are inundated with resumes and job applications, many of which are fake or inappropriate for the role.

It is critical to leverage your network in the job search, which can be hard if you have spent your entire career within one company.

Hiring managers have changed what they look for, too. AI fluency is becoming table stakes. The “process” of how you build/sell/market with AI is more key than what you build. Candidates are expected to show prototypes and proof of how they use AI tools every day.

The jobs themselves are changing. A friend told me last month that he wanted an engineering manager role. There are fewer manager roles in the market now.

AI has driven a reduction in management layers and a general flattening of organizations. The engineering team at a small AI firm today is a CTO and a group of strong individual contributors. It is normal for managers to have 10 to 30 direct reports now, versus five to 10 in the pre-AI era.

Product management, program management and design teams are shrinking, as well, as AI automates certain jobs.

Sources indicate that hiring managers may view spending your whole career at Microsoft as a yellow flag. Microsoft is an iconic but unusual company. Almost no one else sells to and services customers the way Microsoft does, with an account executive inside nearly every large enterprise in the world.

The skills that get you promoted in Redmond don’t always carry over to a 500- to 5,000-person software tech giant.

It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a manufacturer.

It has been revealed that software is cheap to build now. A product leader and an engineer using AI tools can ship in weeks what used to take a team a year.

This cuts both ways for startups. Every good idea attracts a dozen competitors within months, and the significant platforms will copy anything that works.

The true strength of a startup today is the ability to grow revenue quickly and establish leadership in a beachhead market. The sales, marketing, product-led growth and distribution strategies are becoming the most critical parts of the business.

The bar for venture funding is extremely high. Jason Lemkin of SaaStr recently shared data from ICONIQ showing that top “AI forward” startups under $10 million in annual recurring revenue are growing 900% a year at the median.

One venture investor told me they advise their portfolio companies that if they aren’t on track for a $10 million run rate within two years, they won’t raise another round. Last week I spoke with an investor who owns part of a business with $4 million in revenue, growing 100% a year and losing $1 million, and it can’t raise.

There are three fundraising paths.

1) Think VERY big, raise a lot and grow fast enough to justify it. Build an incredible team pursuing an ambitious idea. Raise a large round based on the promise of becoming the next Anthropic, OpenAI or legal AI startup Harvey. Many of the most interesting companies are not software or AI-related, but are “deep tech” companies in defense, robotics, energy and biotech.

2) Raise a moderate amount of money from angels, family offices and nontraditional funds to build a business that has the ability to be profitable on one round of financing. You can control your destiny by building a company that doesn’t rely on the venture capital funding market.

In a recent development, 3) Bootstrap and build a business that you own. Fund it yourself, grow it with revenue and get to profitability.

The question that most people are NOT asking is: What do I really want?

Before December, block out an afternoon and think about the last time you were happy at work.

It has been revealed that there are many frameworks for figuring out what you want in your career and life in general. I’m a fan of the Four Elements exercise. Write down three times in your career when you felt energized and effective. From those, work out what gives you energy, where you have the most impact, what culture you do best in and what your constraints are: money, kids, aging parents and how many more years you want to work.

On LinkedIn, I have seen examples of Microsoft employees taking the VEO to start their own businesses in property management, buy car washes, take time to recharge, spend time with family and travel.

Other employees are starting the job search in earnest but not taking the VEO. Many others are just getting back to work and doubling down on Microsoft.

According to recent reports, whichever way you go, start now. Start by aligning on your priorities and what you want from your career. If you stay, use the next year to build your skills with AI and to grow a network outside Redmond. If you leave to build something, decide early which of the three funding paths you’re on, because that choice shapes everything that follows.

The people I’ve watched land well after Big Tech had one thing in common: they knew what they wanted before they walked out the door, whether that was a newly introduced role, a firm of their own or a year with their family.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a week after Binance suffered the biggest cyberattack seen in the history of the crypto market, the onchain monitoring platform Whale Alert has spotted the hacker moving some of the funds in large quantities.

The transfer has raised concerns across the crypto community about what the hacker might be up to and about the possibility of Binance recovering the stolen funds, especially after they are moved to another wallet.

Although the source did not provide sufficient details about the highly concerning transfer, it demonstrated that the attacker behind the 2026 Binance hack moved 60,000 ETH on Wednesday in 2026.

The broader crypto market has continued to suffer extreme volatility since the attack happened in late October. Hence, the total portion of Ethereum tokens transferred from the stolen stash is now worth $108.78 million at ETH’s current market price.

While the reason behind the sudden move after a few weeks of silence remains uncertain, further data demonstrated that the assets were moved in five separate transfers of 12,000 ETH each.

Notably, each transaction was worth between $21.75 million and $21.77 million, and they were identified as Binance’s stolen funds because they were all moved from a wallet labeled 'Binance hack' in 2026.

Considering the history of the transferred funds, the move has sparked speculation that the hacker might already be preparing to spend the stolen funds, further sabotaging Binance’s chances of full recovery.

However, it is notable to note that there is no evidence that the attacker has sold the Ethereum, as the receiving wallet has not been identified.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Just as the Industrial Revolution transformed business through machines, mass production and long-distance transportation, AI may be powering a upcoming entrepreneurial boom.

Industry observers note that we’ve seen this before: New technology dramatically lowers the cost of starting and running a business. But where the steam engine and electricity offered only a first step, still requiring substantial capital for machinery, factories and workers, AI offers modern entrepreneurs a full staircase. Today, an aspiring founder with a good idea can access powerful capabilities with little more than a computer and a Wi-Fi connection. The challenge is knowing what you need to launch and grow a business at each stage.

In a recent development, business creation has surged in 2026, with nearly every month setting a record for new registrations compared with the same month in previous years. Since January, 5.9 million new businesses have been formed nationwide — up 16% from the same period in 2025 and 24% from 2024.

What’s driving that growth? It’s not a single engine but a combination of forces, including the continued popularity of remote work and the appeal of being your own boss and having more financial freedom, both now more within reach because of AI.

According to recent reports, if you previously dropped a business idea because it seemed too complicated or expensive, now may be the time to reconsider. AI has reached a level of capability that didn’t exist just a few years ago. It’s steadily eroding traditional startup barriers, helping founders turn even ambitious ideas into real businesses with less money, fewer employees and fewer outside resources.

It has been revealed that until recently, launching a firm often meant spending money before making money. Office space, equipment, expensive software and employees with specialized skills were requirements in most sectors, not to mention the accountants and consultants needed just to get started.

It has been revealed that now, cloud infrastructure has replaced costly servers. No-code platforms make it possible to build websites and apps without extensive programming knowledge. E-commerce platforms give small companies access to national and global markets. Generative AI accelerates this trend by helping entrepreneurs research markets, analyze competitors, draft business plans, develop marketing campaigns, create content and automate tedious administrative work.

Recent findings suggest that start by asking yourself, “What do I need to reach customers at this stage, and how will it maximize my return on investment?” Use inexpensive tools to create a product prototype, a landing page or a basic marketing campaign. Talk to potential customers. Test your pricing and measure the response. Save major investments for ideas that show real demand.

AI gives founders a chance to rethink hiring. Entrepreneurs once had to hire employees or contractors before they were generating enough revenue to support them. Today, a solo founder with the right AI tools can handle many of those functions alone.

That doesn’t mean putting complete trust in a chatbot. AI-assisted work still requires human oversight, judgment, verification and refinement. And when you’re building a trustworthy brand from scratch, you have to consider accuracy, privacy and legal issues.

It has been revealed that use AI to draft routine marketing emails, but hire an experienced marketer when strategy matters. Organize basic finances with bookkeeping software, but consult an accountant for important tax decisions. Automate answers to repetitive customer service questions, but keep a human in the loop for complicated interactions or when customers ask for one. The goal isn’t to eliminate employees. It’s to delay fixed expenses until your business can support them.

Sources indicate that historically, founders moved to places like San Francisco or Austin because those cities offered concentrated pools of money and talent. Those hubs remain vibrant, but AI and remote technology are reducing the importance of location.

A tech founder in a small town can use the same AI platforms and cloud services as someone in Silicon Valley. Remote collaboration provides access to talent anywhere, and e-commerce can reach customers far beyond a company’s hometown.

In a recent development, with AI tools, you can explore many ideas from almost anywhere. Instead of asking, “Where does my business need to be based?” you can ask, “Where would I like to live while I grow my business?” That kind of freedom can make a real difference in your quality of life.

Forming a business and building a successful one are different things. Many of the companies registered this year will never become fully operational. Others will struggle to find customers or stay profitable. AI can’t fix a weak business model, create demand where none exists or eliminate the financial risks of entrepreneurship.

According to recent reports, what AI can do is make the process easier and cheaper, and therein lies the lesson. Instead of investing heavily up front in one untested concept, make a series of small bets. Develop a minimum viable product. Test marketing messages. Experiment with prices. Ask AI to identify the assumptions in your business blueprint, then test them with real customers and real-world data.

Industry observers note that with more than 5 million businesses formed since the start of 2026, the U.S. could finish the year with close to 7 million latest registrations if the current pace continues. There’s evidence that AI may be contributing to that momentum. But like the steam engine, electricity, the internet and smartphones before it, AI is a tool. The real power lies with entrepreneurs who are willing to start lean, test early, automate selectively and spend strategically. With that approach, we may see a boom not only in startups with potential but, more importantly, in businesses that endure.

  • In a recent development, the limitations have been understood for some time.
  • Sources indicate that for founders, this is worth paying attention to now rather than later.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in October, reports that OpenAI‘s annualized revenue was running well below earlier estimates sent AI-linked stocks sharply lower and prompted a fresh round of scrutiny over AI valuations. It also reopened a question investors have been circling for a while: Is ARR still the right way to describe an AI business?

In a recent development, the limitations have been understood for some time. ARR was built for software companies selling predictable annual contracts, which is only part of how most AI companies make money. Through the early part of the generative AI boom, growth was steep enough that few people pressed the point. The OpenAI episode has made it harder to leave alone, partly because it demonstrated how much weight public markets now place on a single private firm’s numbers.

Sources indicate that for founders, this is worth paying attention to now rather than later. A cohort of AI companies is reaching the growth-capital stage, and the questions they face in diligence are changing.

Industry observers note that ARR became standard in the mid- to late-2000s, when software moved from licence fees to recurring subscriptions. A customer signed for 12 months, revenue became predictable and annualizing it was arithmetic rather than forecasting.

The first generation of post-ChatGPT companies inherited it without much examination, despite earning money in a different way. Most now run hybrid models: a subscription base with consumption charges on top, billed against API calls, tokens processed or compute used. A growing number charge per outcome. An annualized figure blends revenue a customer has committed to with revenue that depends on what they use next month.

What gets presented as ARR is usually a revenue run rate: recent revenue multiplied out to an annual figure. That is a reasonable way to describe momentum, and a less reliable guide to the year ahead. The first question an investor tends to ask is what the figure actually counts.

It has been revealed that companies that sell partly through partners can report either the full value of those sales or only the share they keep, and the two conventions produce very different numbers for the same business. Both are legitimate, but the two are not necessarily comparable.

Take two companies both reporting a $10 million annualized run rate. In the first, most of that revenue is contracted, and comes from customers whose usage has expanded steadily over 12 months. In the second, it rests on a handful of customers whose consumption spiked in the last quarter.

These are not similar businesses. The first has demonstrated that customers keep coming back and spending more. Nothing in the headline figure tells you that.

Sources indicate that if a single figure cannot separate those two businesses, the question is what can. The answer depends on the stage. At pre-seed and seed, the number matters. A steep trajectory can point to market demand, to customers willing to pay, and to a team beginning to crack go-to-market. A run rate isn’t generally expected to predict the year at that size.

Industry observers note that later you need more. What matters is the revenue behind the number: customer concentration, how much is contracted rather than consumed, how predictable that revenue is, and whether the gross margins hold as volume rises.

Industry observers note that retention and expansion are the centerpiece. They tell you how essential a product has become and whether it will still be in use in a few years. Churn is diagnostic in a way a growth figure never is. It can point to demand the product is not answering, pricing that does not match the value, a need that was never really recurring, or a market shallower than it first looked.

ARR has been a staple of how high-growth tech companies demonstrate momentum for such a long time that it’s not likely to disappear anytime soon.

It has been revealed that what is changing is how much weight that single number can carry on its own. Expect more investors to ask what a figure actually counts, how much of it is committed revenue, and what retention looks like by cohort. The founders who have those answers ready will tell a much more convincing story than a single number ever could.

Industry observers note that kenza Zayani is an early-stage investor at RTP Global, based in London. She is drawn to ambitious founders tackling the most challenging problems, with a particular interest in AI from infrastructure to applications. Zayani has built experience in venture capital across stages, and at RTP Global, she brings her multistage experience and data-driven approach to company building with founders.

  • It has been revealed that the investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S.
  • It has been revealed that india has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bharat Semi, an Indian semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as it seeks to win customers in the United States and elsewhere.

It has been revealed that the investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology firm General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon. Its image sensors, however, remain under development, with the startup targeting its initial commercial production in 2027.

It has been revealed that india has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S. companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. The country, however, has yet to establish itself as a major chip manufacturing hub. Meanwhile, the AI boom is also giving Indian startups such as Bharat Semi an opportunity to develop specialized chips for global markets.

In a recent development, the Latest Delhi-based startup is developing programmable image sensors that combine image capture, processing, and AI capabilities on a single chip, reducing the need to send visual data to separate processors. The move could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with conventional setups that use a separate image sensor, image signal processor, and a system-on-chip, co-founder Vrinda Kapoor (pictured above, right) said in an interview.

“Our aim here is to move from sensors to sense-making solutions,” Kapoor told TechCrunch.

According to recent reports, kapoor, a South Park Commons fellow who earlier worked in healthcare technology, co-founded Bharat Semi in late 2021 with Vinayak Dalmia (pictured above, left), the startup’s managing director, who previously worked at McKinsey and in private equity. Its chief technology officer, Boyd Fowler, previously held the same role at image-sensor maker OmniVision.

Recent findings suggest that bharat Semi is targeting smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance, and aerospace. Without disclosing specifics, Kapoor pointed to air conditioners that could detect when a room is empty and adjust automatically and drones that could process visual information — even with the absence of more expensive computing hardware elsewhere in the system.

The startup’s first-generation sensors are already in prototyping, while its second-generation sensors, which will incorporate more advanced AI capabilities, are expected to reach the prototype stage by mid-2027, Kapoor mentioned. Moreover, the startup plans to get those newer sensors into customers’ hands by the end of 2027.

Sources indicate that the all-equity seed round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indusbridge Ventures, with participation from Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels, and individual investors. Bharat Semi, Kapoor said, prepares to use the funding to expand its engineering team, complete product development, and bring its sensors to market.

Bharat Semi has about 75 employees across India and the U.S., including 10 to 12 in its American operations, which span engineering and business development in Santa Clara. The startup prepares to increase its U.S. headcount to around 20 by mid-2027, Kapoor said. It has also begun hiring engineers in Europe.

“It’s a story of can we build a global technology tech giant out of India,” Kapoor stated.

In 2024, Bharat Semi declared intends for a semiconductor fabrication project in India involving a technology partnership with the U.S. Space Force. The initiative, Kapoor stated, remains in development and the startup is working to identify domestic partners that would build and operate the facility.

In a recent development, the project is separate from Bharat Semi’s image-sensor business, Kapoor added. The startup plans to remain fabless, outsourcing chip manufacturing while focusing on semiconductor design and software. The latest funding will not be used to finance the proposed fabrication facility.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.
  • At the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot highlights its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT.
  • Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

At the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot highlights its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

Blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham notes those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

Industry observers note that if Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

It has been revealed that the FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

It highlights how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own users. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

While the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now shows:.

Sources indicate that the first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what owners hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:.

Why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:.

Asset | Held with third-party custodians.

The striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, showed BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:.

It has been revealed that not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

How Binance indicates it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:.

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

It has been revealed that what the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It highlights the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance claims the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest patch says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:.

The design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

In a recent development, what it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

What customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Sources indicate that binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

In a recent development, bitcoin price has fallen below $62,000 for the first time since early July, extending a brutal November selloff as institutional investors pull billions from the market. BTC touched $61,270 just now, before recovering slightly to trade around $61,700.

According to recent reports, bitcoin price has now lost more than 10% over seven days, with selling pressure spreading across equities, precious metals and other risk assets. Yesterday’s $582.2 million outflow from US spot Bitcoin ETFs added another blow, bringing November withdrawals close to $3.5 billion.

Sources indicate that blackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest single-day outflow since launching. The same session saw $727 million in crypto liquidations, with bullish traders absorbing most of the damage.

Institutional demand is weakening, leveraged buyers are being forced out, and the Federal Reserve’s increasingly hawkish outlook is making speculative assets less attractive.

Bitcoin is now approaching $60,000, a level that could determine if the correction finds a floor or develops into something uglier.

According to recent reports, the ETF withdrawals are arguably the biggest concern for Bitcoin holders right now. Spot Bitcoin ETFs became an crucial source of institutional demand after launching in January 2024. Their buying helped absorb available supply and gave traditional investors a regulated route into the market.

According to recent reports, that demand is now moving in the opposite direction. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $1.1 billion this week alone. November’s cumulative withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion.

Industry observers note that the pressure extends beyond ETFs. Rising Treasury yields and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase in December have encouraged investors to reduce exposure to assets that offer no regular income.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, derivatives traders are taking heavy losses. CoinGlass data demonstrated more than $700 million in liquidations across crypto markets over 24 hours. Long positions accounted for 86% of the total.

Bitcoin itself recorded nearly $202 million in liquidations, with bullish traders suffering the majority of forced closures.

This creates a difficult environment for buyers. Falling prices trigger liquidations, which create additional selling pressure and push prices lower. The reduction in open interest also suggests excessive leverage is being flushed from the market.

Recent findings suggest that the immediate battle is around $60,000. Bitcoin needs to reclaim $62,000 and establish support above it before bulls can confidently argue that the latest breakdown was temporary.

There are three possible scenarios:.

Scenario 1: Bitcoin loses $60K and heads toward $58K or $53K.

Industry observers note that this is the bearish outcome. A decisive break below $60,000 could trigger another wave of stop-loss orders and leveraged liquidations.

The next downside area sits around $58,000, while more aggressive technical projections point toward $53,700.

The daily chart offers little encouragement for bulls. Bitcoin trades below its major moving averages, while bearish momentum continues to dominate. A sustained recovery in ETF flows would become increasingly important to prevent further deterioration.

Scenario 2: Bitcoin stabilizes between $60K and $62K.

This would give buyers time to absorb available supply without immediately reversing the entire November decline.

Industry observers note that the liquidation wave has already removed considerable leverage from the market. If ETF withdrawals begin slowing, Bitcoin could establish a trading range before attempting another recovery.

But sideways trading alone would not confirm a bottom. Buyers need to demonstrate that they can defend support through multiple sessions.

Scenario 3: Bitcoin reclaims $62K and introduces a relief rally.

Sources indicate that A recovery above $62,000 would provide the first meaningful sign that sellers are losing control. A move toward $65,000 would then become possible, followed by resistance around $68,000.

Consistent ETF inflows, improving market sentiment, and a weaker dollar would strengthen this scenario. Without those developments, any rebound risks becoming another opportunity for sellers to exit.

For existing holders, the decision depends heavily on their entry price, investment horizon, and exposure. Long-term holders who bought substantially below current prices have more room to withstand volatility. Selling simply because Bitcoin crossed a psychological threshold risks locking in profits or losses without knowing whether the broader investment thesis has changed.

However, investors holding leveraged positions face a different problem. Falling prices can trigger forced liquidations regardless of their long-term convictions. Reducing leverage and protecting available capital should take priority over waiting for a rebound.

It has been revealed that for buyers, the temptation to buy the dip is understandable. Bitcoin is considerably cheaper than it was just weeks ago, but cheaper does not automatically mean undervalued.

Buying in stages rather than committing an entire allocation around $61,000 offers more flexibility if the market tests $58,000 or even $53,700.

Industry observers note that bitcoin price remains vulnerable to another leg down. The $60,000 level is no longer just a psychological milestone. It is where the next major battle between buyers and sellers.

Amazon threatens to leave NYC again, this time over delivery bill, as it rallies customers to fight it

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:02 amNovember 19, 2026 at 10:56 am.
  • The Seattle tech giant is threatening to move its delivery operations out of the city over a proposed law that would require it to directly employ the drivers who bring packages to Latest Yorkers’ doors.
  • The legislation, known as the Delivery Protection Act or Intro 518, would apply to companies that run last-mile delivery facilities in the city.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:02 amNovember 19, 2026 at 10:56 am.

Amazon and Fresh York City are fighting again.

The Seattle tech giant is threatening to move its delivery operations out of the city over a proposed law that would require it to directly employ the drivers who bring packages to Latest Yorkers’ doors. It’s also asking its customers to help fight the bill.

The legislation, known as the Delivery Protection Act or Intro 518, would apply to companies that run last-mile delivery facilities in the city. Amazon is the main target, but FedEx and several regional couriers would also be covered.

Industry observers note that companies would need a license from the city’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, which would also investigate complaints. The bill was introduced in February.

On Thursday, Amazon began showing New York City customers pop-up messages and a homepage banner that reads, “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order. Act now to protect low prices.” The notices link to a form and a pre-written letter customers can send to their council members to oppose the bill, Bloomberg reported. Amazon pointed GeekWire to a study by consulting firm AKRF estimating the bill would raise consumer costs by $409 to $664 a year, but didn’t detail how it arrived at the per-order figure.

According to recent reports, in a blog post, Amazon said it relies on a network of small delivery businesses in the city. “If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city,” the firm wrote. “That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.”.

Industry observers note that amazon debuted its Delivery Service Partners program in 2018, letting entrepreneurs start their own companies to deliver Amazon packages in Amazon-branded vans and uniforms. The companies hire their own drivers, while Amazon pays them to deliver and offers discounts on vehicles, fuel and insurance. The model lets Amazon expand its delivery network without directly employing drivers.

Sources indicate that in a statement to GeekWire, Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel remarked the bill “as written” would threaten more than 40 small delivery businesses the company works with in the city and the more than 5,000 New Yorkers they employ. More than 2,000 Amazon employees also work at its delivery facilities in the city, the company said.

Industry observers note that “We’re hopeful this bill doesn’t pass as written,” Nantel stated. “But so far, key City Council members seem uninterested in learning about our delivery operations.” Amazon said neither Council Member Tiffany Cabán, the bill’s sponsor, nor Mayor Zohran Mamdani has accepted its offer to visit a delivery facility. The company also said customers sent about 20,000 emails to council members within six hours of the campaign’s launch Thursday morning.

The standoff echoes Amazon’s 2019 reversal on its second headquarters. That February, the organization abruptly canceled looks to build a 25,000-person “HQ2” office in Long Island City, Queens, after more than a year of competition among cities to host it. Amazon blamed “a number of state and local politicians” who opposed the project, which drew fierce criticism over roughly $3 billion in government incentives.

Industry observers note that amazon stuck with its plans for Arlington, Va., and Nashville and didn’t reopen its search. Polls at the time highlighted most Newly introduced Yorkers supported the deal, but Queens officials, labor leaders and activists fought it. State Sen. Michael Gianaris, who led the opposition, accused Amazon of trying to shake down governments to get its way.

It defies logic that Amazon, a $3 trillion corporation, would raise Newly introduced Yorkers’ cost of living if it’s forced to adhere to basic regulations and worker protections.We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs.If… https://t.co/UWXVTJhRL6.

City leaders backing the delivery bill see a familiar pattern. “Amazon is once again making spurious attacks against this commonsense legislation that would make workers and our streets safer,” noted Cabán, the bill’s sponsor, who called Amazon’s warning a “dishonest scare tactic.”.

City Council Speaker Julie Menin questioned Amazon’s cost claims in a post on X.

“It defies logic that Amazon, a $3 trillion corporation, would raise New Yorkers’ cost of living if it’s forced to adhere to basic regulations and worker protections,” she wrote, adding that the council is “crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs.”.

Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon’s subcontractor model “leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets,” CNBC reported.

Supporters, including the Teamsters union, which has sought to organize Amazon drivers and warehouse workers, say the bill would make the work safer and make it harder for Amazon to distance itself from driver injuries.

According to recent reports, amazon disputes that the bill would improve safety. The firm stated it has invested more than $2.5 billion in driver safety since 2019, that the serious crash rate for its drivers in New York City fell 35.7% from 2024 to 2025, and that drivers there have averaged nearly $24 an hour since January 2025, with required health coverage and paid time off.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, business groups have run ads against the bill and warned they may sue the city if it passes, according to CNBC. The measure is awaiting review by Menin.

Bitcoin's 200-week moving average (200WMA) has climbed above $68,000 for the first time, Blockstream CEO Adam Back noted on X on Nov. 18. "Bitcoin passes $68k 200wma," he wrote. Back attached a 200-week moving average heatmap from Look Into Bitcoin, and the chart shows the indicator rising throughout Bitcoin's history. On Nov. 18, the indicator was between $67,955 and $68,145.

#bitcoin passes $68k 200wma https://t.co/dgIzS9Nsvw https://t.co/xzYdP0EvZh.

Back is the cryptographer behind Hashcash. The algorithm laid the groundwork for proof-of-work, and Satoshi Nakamoto cited it in the Bitcoin white paper. Back was also one of the first people Satoshi contacted before the launch of Bitcoin in 2009.

According to recent reports, the Blockstream CEO has posted about the 200WMA on X several times this year. On March 27, he wrote that the "200wma passes $59k." The indicator was just above $60,000 in early May, and on May 30, Back reported that it had crossed $61,000. In September, the 200WMA rose above $65,000 for the first time.

In a follow-up post in May, Back cited a maxim of the late Charlie Munger. According to Munger, an investor who buys only high-quality assets when they trade at the 200-week moving average would beat the S&P 500 over time. Back also noted that Munger and Warren Buffett never embraced Bitcoin.

In a recent development, in mid-September, Bitcoin was trading at around $76,000 to $77,000. At that time, the gap between the price and the 200WMA was more than $10,000.

Sources indicate that on Wednesday, Bitcoin was trading at $64,150, about 6% below the 200WMA. On Nov. 15, BTC dropped as low as $62,000 before bouncing 5.5%. Back called the move "bouncy" in a post on X.

In a CNBC interview on Nov. 12, Back noted that Bitcoin could reach $1 million by 2028. According to Back, more than 95% of potential institutional inflows into Bitcoin are still ahead. He named investment trusts, asset managers and corporate treasuries among the buyers, and he said that their buying was just beginning.

Back also pointed to the Bitcoin halving in the spring of 2028. He mentioned that miners would sell fewer coins after it.

He made a similar point at Paris Blockchain Week in April. "When the Bitcoin price is low, the miners have to sell a bigger proportion… and when the price is higher, they don't have to sell as much," Back stated at the time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Industry observers note that most entrepreneurs are using AI to get work done faster. But what if it’s moving their businesses in the wrong direction?

AI can now help entrepreneurs produce marketing campaigns, research competitors, develop strategies and complete work that once took entire teams. It’s an extraordinary shift in what’s possible for a small business. But there’s a hidden risk in all that productivity. In the video above, I explore why the entrepreneurs who gain the greatest advantage from AI aren’t the ones doing more work, but the ones discovering opportunities everyone else overlooks.

That’s what I call the “Progress Illusion.” When AI makes completing tasks effortless, it’s tempting to mistake activity for achievement. But there’s a difference between the work AI completes, how customers respond, the business results that follow and the longer-term consequences. These are the four dominoes that determine whether all that activity is actually moving your business forward.

Finished is a status. Progress is a consequence.

Industry observers note that consider a surprising study of eBay’s paid search advertising. When the manufacturer stopped running ads for searches containing its own name, researchers found that 99.5% of the lost paid-ad traffic was replaced by free search traffic. Now imagine using AI to scale that campaign because the dashboard looked impressive. You wouldn’t necessarily be scaling growth. You could be scaling waste.

The opportunity for entrepreneurs is to use AI for something far more powerful than execution: strategic foresight.

According to recent reports, in the video, I walk through AHEAD, my five-step framework for challenging assumptions, exploring new possibilities and uncovering business opportunities you might otherwise overlook. But even smart analysis has its limits. AI can generate so many competing strategies that deciding what to do becomes a job in itself. That’s the “Analysis Trap.”.

Industry observers note that the solution is knowing when to stop researching and start acting. I call it the “Decision Line”: three questions that help you determine whether you need stronger evidence or whether it’s time to make your next move.

Because your most valuable opportunity might not be the one you’re already pursuing. It could be an entirely different direction you haven’t considered. And you don’t need a Fortune 500 strategy department to start thinking more strategically about your business.

AI can help you execute almost any plan. The real competitive advantage is discovering which plan deserves to be executed.

And in the video above, I’ll show you how to start thinking differently, uncover opportunities others overlook and make your next business move with greater confidence.

The free AI Success Kit, available to download for a limited time, comes with a free chapter from my fresh book, The Wolf is at The Door – How to Survive and Thrive in an AI-Driven World.

The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq tomorrow with a growth story that’s unlike any I’ve seen in close to three decades working in Silicon Valley: The tech giant says revenue reached $17 billion in Q3, less than four years after Claude debuted with zero.
  • The San Francisco-based organization also presents a stark contrast to the more common theme in recent years of venture-backed companies staying private longer: Anthropic is less than six years old as it goes public in a potentially record-setting listing.
  • Those metrics are impressive, but there are other numbers in its S-1 I keep circling, too, like the nearly $900 billion in compute purchase and lease commitments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq tomorrow with a growth story that’s unlike any I’ve seen in close to three decades working in Silicon Valley: The tech giant says revenue reached $17 billion in Q3, less than four years after Claude debuted with zero.

The San Francisco-based organization also presents a stark contrast to the more common theme in recent years of venture-backed companies staying private longer: Anthropic is less than six years old as it goes public in a potentially record-setting listing.

Those metrics are impressive, but there are other numbers in its S-1 I keep circling, too, like the nearly $900 billion in compute purchase and lease commitments.

Sources indicate that I’ve worked in Silicon Valley through the dot-com boom and bust, the rise of SaaS, social media, unicorn and decacorn startups and now, AI. Anthropic’s extraordinary rise and entrance onto the public markets marks a new technology era — one with enormous growth and potential, but also tremendous costs, risks and unknowns.

OpenAI’s seminal success was the launch of chatbots in 2022 — within two months, ChatGPT reached 100 million owners and in less than four years, OpenAI had a billion monthly active users.

By contrast, Anthropic’s breakout was the success of Claude Code, introduced just last year. Already, Anthropic states 11,900 companies use the product, spending $100,000 or more trailing 12 months, up 12x from a year ago. In its S-1, the firm says that marks the fastest enterprise adoption for any company on record.

Anthropic’s IPO could value it at $1.4 trillion and raise $88.5 billion via the IPO and concurrent private placement. As it becomes public, I’ll be watching closely to see if the manufacturer can keep turning demand for Claude and Claude Code into a durable business while building out the astounding amount of compute it says it needs and managing the many risks that surround its technology.

Here are some of the other key details and figures that caught my eye ahead of Anthropic’s first day on the public markets:.

Anthropic got to where it is now through a fast sequence of funding rounds, from its Jaan Tallinn-led Series A in 2021 to its Series H in May of this year that valued the company at $965 billion.

Other lead investors over its many funding rounds include Google, Amazon, Spark Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Coatue and Sequoia Capital, all of whom are slated to be among the winners when it goes public tomorrow.

Recent findings suggest that the AI era has the potential to generate massive amounts of latest wealth and unlock life-changing technological advances. But it also comes with huge risks. Anthropic’s S-1 captures that tension.

The opportunity the company describes extends far beyond coding and software. It notes its focus in 2027 will be AI agents for knowledge work and scientific discovery. It also points to potential gains in biology and rare-disease research, economic growth, wider access to health care and improved government services. The S-1 cites the World Health Organization’s estimate that 4.6 billion people lack access to basic health services.

That promise comes with a competitive risk for its customers, too: Companies may worry that data they share with AI providers could help train models that compete with their products, or that more capable models could erode parts of their existing businesses.

Anthropic’s S-1 also flags risks ranging from cyber and biological attacks to unpredictable model behavior, authoritarian surveillance and economic disruption.

Sources indicate that anthropic’s public-benefit structure is meant to balance those competing pressures. As a public benefit corporation, the manufacturer states it must weigh commercial success against the public good. Its founders, employees and Long-Term Benefit Trust share in governance; the trust has no financial stake and weighs impacts on national security, economics, global health and science. Anthropic points to its launch of Mythos as an example of that balance.

As Anthropic debuts tomorrow, I’ll be watching how well it balances AI’s promise with the risks its own filing lays out.

Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dreamteam, a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge.
  • Recent findings suggest that the funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest.
  • Sources indicate that traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dreamteam, a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge.

Recent findings suggest that the funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest. The San Francisco-based startup declined to disclose the size of each round or its valuation.

Sources indicate that traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date. That often leaves businesses with incomplete or outdated information. Dreamteam aims to eliminate much of that work by automatically capturing context from sources including emails and customer conversations. It also uses AI agents to handle tasks such as follow-ups, meeting preparation, and pipeline monitoring.

In a recent development, dreamteam co-founder and CEO Anand Venkatraman (pictured above, right) told TechCrunch that he had repeatedly encountered problems with traditional CRM platforms over more than 25 years in enterprise software, including at Salesforce and Freshworks. Salespeople spent considerable time updating records, yet managers still struggled to get a reliable picture of their business. “In all these years, I have never come across an instance where I could click a button and get a forecast from the CRM,” he mentioned.

That experience led Venkatraman to co-found Dreamteam in 2025 with Senthil Kanthaswamy (pictured above, center), who spent more than nine years at Freshworks, most recently as a product leader at Freshservice, and Ramesh Parthasarathy (pictured above, left), who previously worked on AI and platform engineering at Freshworks.

Industry observers note that at the heart of Dreamteam’s CRM is what it calls the Company Brain. This acts as virtual memory, pulling together information from emails, meetings, and other customer interactions to build a shared record of customer relationships. Four built-in AI agents use that information to research prospects, draft follow-up emails, flag potential risks to deals, and configure CRM workflows, with sales teams retaining control over what gets sent to customers.

Sources indicate that dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries in the three months since it began actively selling its product, with most paying for the service, Venkatraman said. The startup has also replaced established CRM platforms at several businesses, including Salesforce at healthcare company DMS Health and HubSpot at other customers.

Recent findings suggest that the advertising sales team at media streaming manufacturer Plex also chose Dreamteam over HubSpot and other AI-native CRM alternatives, Venkatraman told TechCrunch. Plex’s co-founder and chief product officer Scott Olechowski remarked Dreamteam’s ability to integrate with AI tools already used across the company was a “game changer.”.

Recent findings suggest that replacing established CRM platforms at scale may prove more difficult. In a blog post earlier this year, venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) argued that while AI could transform how businesses manage customer relationships, existing CRMs are likely to remain the systems where customer records are stored, with a new generation of AI-powered tools capturing much of the value by working on top of them.

Venkatraman acknowledged that Salesforce and HubSpot are unlikely to disappear anytime soon, but noted that their entrenched positions do not guarantee they will dominate the next generation of CRM software.

“We see this as an electric-car moment for systems of record,” he said, adding that AI requires a fundamental rethink of how CRMs are built — not simply adding new features to existing platforms.

According to recent reports, kanthaswamy believes startups have a window of two to five years to gain ground before established CRM providers can fully adapt to AI. Rebuilding software around a fundamentally different architecture takes time, he stated, giving newer companies an opportunity to attract customers while incumbents work to overhaul their existing products.

Dreamteam also plans to expand beyond sales into other parts of the customer lifecycle, including onboarding, customer support, and upselling. The startup already has a feature called Magic Apps that allows owners to create custom applications and dashboards within the CRM using natural-language instructions, without writing code.

Presently, Dreamteam employs more than 35 people, with its engineering team based in Chennai and its go-to-market operations in the United States. Kanthaswamy noted the startup aims to reach eight figures in annual revenue by the end of 2027, though he declined to disclose the startup’s current revenue.

Yield-Bearing eZAR Blurs the Line Between Stablecoin and Investment Product

💡 Key Takeaways
  • eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation.
  • According to recent reports, most stablecoin rolls out promise a token that never moves.
  • Recent findings suggest that according to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to new institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation. Its reserve yield is the feature that puts the stablecoin label to the test.

According to recent reports, most stablecoin rolls out promise a token that never moves. eZAR's disclosures say its holders can make money or lose it. The rand-pegged token went live to the public on November 2, and its fine print reads more like an investment product than a payments coin.

Recent findings suggest that according to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to new institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations. The organization notes R303 million worth of tokens had been issued and were in circulation as of October 30.

In a recent development, the project is a partnership between eZAR Ltd, asset manager Ninety One and AVBOB Financial Services, with AVBOB acting as lead institution and liquidity partner. CEO Sean Emery noted the team put "getting it right" ahead of "getting it substantial" during the pilot. The message now is that eZAR is ready to scale.

The model also departs from the typical single-issuer coin. Neobanks, retailers, insurers and payment firms can plug the token into their own branded wallets and share in the economics. Transfers between participating wallets settle within seconds at any hour and, according to the firm, cost nothing.

The reserves backing eZAR are invested through a money market strategy run by Ninety One, mainly in the Ninety One Money Market Fund. Returns are distributed daily to partners after partnership fees, and each partner then decides on what terms its own customers receive a share.

Recent findings suggest that ninety One's head of digital assets, Adam Duxbury, described it as fresh rails under an old discipline. His firm has run money market strategies for 25 years, he noted, and South Africa should build its own digital rand rather than import a dollar coin.

The framing is clever, since it presents the yield as a feature of "digital cash that can grow." Yet that same feature makes the classification question hard to avoid.

The risk language is the most revealing part of the launch. eZAR describes itself as a crypto asset issued by the eZAR En Commandite Partnership. It states that the token is not legal tender, not a bank deposit and not a banking product, and that it carries no guarantee.

The details that follow set it further apart. The R1 redemption value depends on available liquidity. Money market returns can be positive or negative, so capital is at risk. Holders also own no units in the underlying fund and have no direct claim on it.

According to recent reports, "Capital at risk" rarely appears in stablecoin terms. A payments token is meant to hold its value and let customers redeem at par, yet eZAR's own documents hedge on both counts. Back in March, a market survey from Blockhouse had already noted that eZAR doesn't qualify as a stablecoin under most regulations. The live launch now tests that observation against a real product.

Recent findings suggest that in the major rulebooks, the yield is the sticking point. The US GENIUS Act bars permitted payment stablecoin issuers from paying holders any form of interest or yield solely for holding, using or retaining the token. The EU's MiCA framework takes a similar line on interest. The logic is that a payment token paying a return starts to function like an unregulated deposit.

The OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rules on October 21, and they confirmed that ban for covered issuers. The contested ground lies elsewhere, in who sits between the issuer and the holder. Earlier OCC proposals set a rebuttable presumption against yield arrangements run through affiliates and related third parties, whereas the statute itself names only issuers.

According to recent reports, eZAR's design lands squarely in that gray zone. Returns flow to partners, and the partners decide how customers share in them. Whether that amounts to an issuer paying yield or a partner passing on profit is precisely the kind of question US regulators are now wrestling with, and it would be a difficult one to argue before the OCC.

eZAR doesn't operate under the US or EU regimes, so none of those rules apply to it directly. eZAR Ltd is described as an authorised financial services provider responsible for the main technology and services behind the partnership. That technology also draws on the South African Reserve Bank's Project Khokha 2, where eZAR's parent company, Block Markets Africa, was a technical contributor.

Industry observers note that this background signals a serious, institution-backed build rather than a speculative launch. Even so, the rand stablecoin field is getting crowded. ZARU released earlier this year as an institutional-grade rand coin, and a pattern is emerging of different models competing for the same local payments niche.

According to recent reports, the bigger question is whether South Africa will define stablecoins narrowly, as the US and EU do, or leave room for hybrid products like this one. Because the network is permissioned, the reported circulation figure also rests on company disclosure rather than a public ledger, which makes the regulatory and disclosure framework matter even more.

Recent findings suggest that for everyday users, the appeal is easy to see. A rand token that moves in seconds, costs nothing to send and might earn a daily return makes an attractive pitch. For partners, shared infrastructure with a revenue share offers a way into digital payments without building a coin from scratch.

Recent findings suggest that the trade-off sits in the disclaimers. A holder who treats eZAR like a bank balance could be caught off guard by liquidity-dependent redemption, or by a money market return that dips below zero. That gap between how the product feels and how it is legally defined is where regulators tend to step in.

Industry observers note that eZAR is best understood as a hybrid: a payments token with an investment return attached. It may well succeed on those terms. Still, as more jurisdictions tighten the stablecoin definition around no-yield, par-redemption tokens, products like this will increasingly be judged on what they are rather than what they are called. How South African regulators treat eZAR in the coming months will show which way that debate is heading.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson is signaling a strategic shift in priorities, moving from building the network’s infrastructure to developing products and driving adoption across its extensive ecosystem, with Midnight (NIGHT) at the epicenter.

On a recent podcast, Hoskinson stated, “Now I’m going from building Cardano to building on Cardano.”.

As pointed out by Cardanians, an educational platform focused on Cardano, Hoskinson described Midnight as the vanguard of this new direction, calling it one of the ecosystem’s most exciting products alongside Midnight City.

More notably, the shift does not mean Cardano’s existing roadmap is being abandoned; rather, Hoskinson suggests the focus is increasingly moving toward delivering practical applications that are instrumental in real-world adoption.

Cardano’s treasury has received 23 million ADA following the return of funds originally allocated to Project Catalyst Fund 15 and Input Output’s Catalyst administration contract.

Cardanians acknowledged that the funds were no longer required since Catalyst administration responsibilities transitioned to the Cardano Foundation.

Their return, therefore, restores previously committed ADA to the treasury, making it available for future ecosystem initiatives and community-approved funding proposals.

This development comes days after the rejection of a proposal seeking 22 million ADA to purchase and tokenize copper, showing the governance community’s ability to vet project funding.

On the price action front, Cardano is nearing a potentially decisive technical level, with Market analyst Lana Valentis highlighting that the cryptocurrency is approaching the midline of a descending channel on the weekly timeframe.
