💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months.
  • According to recent reports, most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number.
  • Industry observers note that house of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

According to recent reports, HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

According to recent reports, most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

Industry observers note that house of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Recent findings suggest that everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no latest spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:.

cap(t) = 2.5% − 0.9% × min(t, 24) / 24.

Industry observers note that here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:.

The yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

Industry observers note that newly introduced tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:.

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio.

According to recent reports, the 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

It has been revealed that the formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

It has been revealed that stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every newly introduced token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

It has been revealed that validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to proposal. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

Industry observers note that recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics said the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

Two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a newly introduced proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

Ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to revision their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

Three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

In a recent development, price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chainflip lost nearly $4.86 million after an attacker drained its Ethereum vault.

he exploit targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic signing system rather than a smart contract bug.

The latest incident marks Chainflip’s second major security breach in just over two months.

Chainflip, a decentralized cross-chain swap protocol, has faced another security scare after nearly $4.86 million in crypto was drained from its Ethereum vault in a single transaction. The attacker moved the stolen funds through Tornado Cash within just nine minutes, forcing the protocol to halt deposits, withdrawals, and swaps.

While its team investigates how the funds were taken.

On-chain investigations by Bitquery show that the attacker targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic key system rather than exploiting a bug in its smart contracts.

In a recent development, the attacker first obtained a valid Schnorr signature from the Ethereum Vault’s Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS) aggregate key. This allowed the attacker to pass the vault’s normal signature checks.

On November 21, 2026, a newly funded wallet (0x78fa) called the Vault.transferBatch function. The transaction passed verification and drained all the vault’s available funds in a single move.

The attacker then moved quickly to hide the stolen funds. Within nine minutes, the exploiter swapped the 3,249,631.41 USDC and 758,141.33 USDT for 2,909 ETH (worth around $4.86 million), then sent it to Tornado Cash in 38 separate batches.

Chainflip has not yet confirmed the $4.86 million loss. Instead, the protocol said it was aware of a potential exploit affecting its vaults and moved into full safe mode as a precaution.

We’re aware of a potential exploit affecting Chainflip vaults.As a precaution, the protocol is being put into full safe mode. Deposits, withdrawals, swaps and quoting are disabled.We’re investigating and will share updates here as we learn more.

“Deposits, withdrawals, swaps, and quoting are disabled; we’re investigating and will share updates here as we learn more.”.

This is Chainflip’s second major attack in just over two months. On September 12, 2026, the protocol lost $736,442 in a separate exploit targeting its TRON integration. That attack was caused by a software flaw in how Chainflip processed TRON transaction data, while the November 21 attack targeted its Ethereum Vault’s cryptographic signing key.

After the September attack, Chainflip paused TRON swaps and used its surplus reserves to fully reimburse affected liquidity providers in USDC.

The protocol has yet to confirm whether it will follow the same recovery strategy for the latest $4.86 million loss.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investment firm Roundhill has suddenly terminated prepares to launch two new XRP- and Solana (SOL)-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

This decision comes after over a year of regulatory filings and multiple delays.

Industry observers note that as per the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings on Nov. 18, Roundhill has officially withdrawn plans to launch the Roundhill XRP Covered Call Strategy ETF and Roundhill Solana Covered Call Strategy ETF.

Interestingly, it submitted the applications for these two funds on Oct. 17, 2025. Therefore, these two funds had been awaiting launch for over 13 months.

As per the latest regulatory filings, Roundhill has been consistently delaying the effective dates for these two funds.

However, instead of launching them, the investment firm has decided to drop both products.

In its requests to withdraw the filings for these funds, Roundhill revealed that it "has no further intention to pursue effectiveness of the Fund." The firm noted that it had not sold any shares under the registrations for these two funds.

Intriguingly, Roundhill failed to elaborate on the sudden decision to axe its aims to launch these two ETFs.

Recent findings suggest that roundhill was planning to launch income-generating XRP and Solana ETFs using a covered call strategy. In such a strategy, investors sell options to earn premiums while also maintaining exposure to the price movements of XRP and Solana.

According to recent reports, unlike spot-based ETFs, these funds would not have held the cryptocurrencies directly. Instead, they would have used options written against existing cryptocurrency ETFs.

According to recent reports, A covered call strategy can be useful for generating regular income. However, it can also cap profits during strong market rallies.

Industry observers note that notably, there has been relatively low demand for income-generating cryptocurrency investment products. This raises concerns about investors' interest in these ETFs.

Surprisingly, this decision came amid substantial net inflows into spot-based XRP and Solana ETFs.

U.S. spot XRP and Solana ETFs recorded net inflows of roughly $969 million between May and October 2026, according to data from SoSoValue.

Overall, these spot ETFs held around $3.26 billion in assets under management as of the end of October.

Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin led the daily ranking of stablecoin inflows into decentralized finance (DeFi), according to Token Terminal data that RWA Foundation shared on X. The DeFi total value locked (TVL) of Ripple's stablecoin grew by $22.3 million over 24 hours, and Tether added $21.6 million. RWA Foundation titled its chart "Ripple led stablecoin DeFi growth.".

In a recent development, paxos, Open Standard and Societe Generale followed with $7.8 million, $4 million and $1.2 million, respectively. World Liberty, United Stables, MetaMask, Tori and Liquity each added less than $700,000 over the same period.

It has been revealed that about $2.8 billion worth of RLUSD is in circulation, compared with about $180 billion worth of Tether's USDT. Tether's stablecoin is still more than 60 times bigger than RLUSD.

According to recent reports, ripple launched RLUSD in December 2024. In mid-September 2026, RLUSD supply passed $2.44 billion, and about $1.38 billion of it was on Ethereum. About $1.05 billion was on the XRP Ledger, Ripple's home network. On Ethereum, the stablecoin is used in DeFi pools on Aave V3, Curve and Morpho.

It has been revealed that RLUSD is issued by Standard Custody & Trust under the supervision of the Upcoming York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), and its reserves are held at custodian bank BNY. In the fall, RLUSD received a Moody's rating and was listed on Coinbase and Robinhood, and Ripple received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Ripple has also integrated RLUSD with payment providers Arf, Convera and Cross River Bank, and the stablecoin is now used in dollar settlements between companies.

According to recent reports, in a CNBC interview on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse called blockchain-based transactions "a wave of emerging technology." "I think 10 years from now you'll see blockchain implemented across our financial infrastructure," he remarked.

Solana has remained one of the major cryptocurrencies that have been heavily affected by the persistent crypto market volatility, stalling demand from both retail and institutional investors.

While Solana has continued to struggle amid the growing market uncertainty, it appears that traders are increasingly exiting their positions even across its DeFi market.

Recent data showcased by blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain shows that two Solana whales unstaked a total of 2.31 million SOL on November 19.

While the total amount of SOL unstaked was worth about $169.4 million, further data indicated that the whales proceeded to transfer the tokens to Coinbase, a leading cryptocurrency exchange in the U.S.

It is important to note that the act of withdrawing SOL previously committed to the network's staking mechanism is regarded as unstaking.

While this move automatically gives holders the ability to transfer, sell, or use the unstaked tokens, the massive unstaking of 2.31 million SOL from large holders has drawn attention within the crypto community regarding the intention behind the move.

With curiosity on the rise about the whales' decision to move such a large amount of SOL to Coinbase Prime, the timing of the move has triggered speculation that the whales may be intending to sell the tokens.

Notably, the move arrived when Solana was trading around $74, briefly shifting into green territory just a few days after it retested $67, the lowest level seen since June 2026.

Since the prolonged price correction has continued to weaken investor confidence, it appears that the whales have acted upon the growing fear and withdrawn the assets they had initially committed to the Solana network to hedge against further losses.

The electric Vespa just got better where it actually matters

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that vespa’s electric scooters have never exactly screamed for attention.
  • But for 2027, Vespa has given its electric lineup a fairly significant technological overhaul while leaving that iconic steel bodywork largely untouched.
  • Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the new electric Vespa lineup now consists of the Primavera Elettrica, Sprint S Elettrica, and the faster Primavera Tech Elettrica.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that vespa’s electric scooters have never exactly screamed for attention. That’s sort of the point. They look like Vespas, ride like Vespas, and just happen to swap the gasoline engine for a much quieter electric drivetrain.

But for 2027, Vespa has given its electric lineup a fairly significant technological overhaul while leaving that iconic steel bodywork largely untouched.

Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the new electric Vespa lineup now consists of the Primavera Elettrica, Sprint S Elettrica, and the faster Primavera Tech Elettrica. And while you’d be forgiven for struggling to spot the differences from across the show floor, there’s a lot more happening underneath.

According to recent reports, the biggest upgrade is an entirely upcoming electric motor developed and manufactured in Italy by Vespa parent firm Piaggio Group. The motor uses a new modular design intended to improve both performance and efficiency, while also doing away with rare-earth materials.

On the 45 km/h (28 mph) Primavera and Sprint S models, Vespa claims the upcoming motor provides stronger acceleration for stop-and-go city riding. Range reaches up to 85 km (53 miles) in Eco mode.

In a recent development, but perhaps the biggest practical improvement is the new removable battery. Being able to pull the battery out of the scooter and carry it inside for charging makes a massive difference for urban riders who don’t have access to a garage or dedicated charging spot – exactly the kind of riders Vespa is targeting.

According to recent reports, the Primavera Tech is where things get a little faster. This version is homologated as a motorcycle rather than a moped in Europe and reaches 67 km/h (42 mph). That’s still not terribly fast, but the electric Vespa line has never been known for its top speed.

Its range has increased by 12.5% thanks to the upcoming motor and Vehicle Management System, reaching 90 km (56 miles) on the WMTC cycle or up to 100 km (62 miles) in Eco mode.

Recent findings suggest that there’s also a latest charger that Vespa indicates reduces energy consumption from the wall by 17%, with a 0-80% charge taking around 2.5 hours. A new Maintenance mode is designed to protect the battery during longer periods when the scooter isn’t being ridden.

Vespa is clearly only really interested in selling their gas models, which come in 50cc, 125cc, & 310cc classes. And the only reason anyone would get a 50cc is if they didn't want to bother to get an actual motorcycle license in some jurisdictions. The electrics are nearly as expensive as the 310s but even the "faster" model only has the power equivalent of about 70cc's. At least the battery in the faster model is now a decent 4.2 kwh, though that one I believe is not removable. Hey I'm actually a Vespa lover I have a 200cc. They are beautiful quality machines, and I don't mind the price premium. But the electrics are quite disappointing, especially for the money. If they had a true 125cc equivalent I would be first in line at the showroom. Very disappointing in that a stouter motor really wouldn't cost them much more at all.

The Primavera Tech also gets the technological bells and whistles you’d expect from the flagship version, including a 5-inch TFT display, keyless operation, navigation through Vespa’s smartphone connectivity system, and remote seat unlocking.

Perhaps the most Vespa thing about the whole update is how little of it you can actually see.

Sources indicate that the company hasn’t tried to turn its electric scooters into rolling science-fiction props. They’re still unmistakably Vespas, complete with the same classic styling that has defined the brand for generations. They just happen to have a much more interesting electric drivetrain hiding underneath now.

Industry observers note that of course, they also carry some very Vespa pricing. While we don’t have word on the updated pricing for the latest models, the outgoing Primavera Elettrica 70 RED was priced at $8,299 in the US. So don’t expect these models to come cheap.

Cotton may be the most dependable fabric for regular every-day t-shirts, but cotton holds onto moisture, which makes it a sweat trap, weighing you down. Instead, opt for synthetic, moisture-wicking fabrics like polyester and nylon that are lighter. They can also be woven in special ways that cotton can't be to enhance breathability. Synthetic fibers don't bleed and are hard to discolor, so they won't get sweat stains. Some menswear brands are even starting to use finely knit wool for its natural breathability, moisture wicking, and odor-fighting properties. Consider what feels best to you and in what environment you might be working out in.

According to recent reports, in most clothing, seams are placed where they are easiest to construct the shirt or look the best. However, those places—like under your armpit and along the side of your body—are also high friction areas, especially when working out. Athletic brands have designed t-shirts that minimize the amount of seams and place them in areas that wont be impacted by your movement. Look out for seams and other high-contact areas that could prose a problem, depending on where they're located.

Simply put, your workout clothes get stinky when they hold on to sweat. A whole range of innovations exist that brands claim will fight odor, but the only sure fire way to keep your workout shirts from stinking are to keep them dry and wash them after every use. That means the workout shirts that retain the least amount of sweat are the easiest to keep from stinking. So if odor is a concern for you (as it should be), look for the shirts that dry the fastest and breath the best. There's a lot of new tech out now that helps combat stink.

Recent findings suggest that forward thinking labels are adding UV protection to workout clothes. Sunscreen is great, but even the best sweat-proof kinds can wear off during long and intense outdoor exercises. Not so with UPF clothing, which block UV rays to keep you protected during your entire sweat session, no reapplication necessary. Even the Skin Cancer Foundation has touted the skin-saving benefits of UPF clothing. If you're looking for even more sun protection, look for long-sleeve t-shirts, or hooded tops with UPF features.

Industry observers note that synthetic fabrics work especially well in workout shirts, as they're designed to handle moisture better than traditional materials. These fabrics include: polyester, Gore-Tex, nylon, and spandex, which have tiny spaces in knit or mesh that allow moisture to move through, evaporating rapidly.

Sources indicate that according to Dr. Corey L. Hartman, MD, an assistant clinical professor of dermatology at the University of Alabama School of Medicine, moisture-wicking fabrics help moisture from the inner layer of the fabric (the part that touches your skin) escape to the outside of the garment.

"Synthetic materials are better at moisture-wicking as they not only pull sweat moisture away from the skin, but they also dry quickly and don’t hold onto moisture," explains. Dr. Marisa Garshick, board-certified dermatologist of MDCS Dermatology.

Sources indicate that "Cotton, on the other hand, while it can absorb sweat and moisture from the skin, it is more likely to hold onto the moisture and not dry as rapidly, leaving the sweat in prolonged contact with the skin," she explains. Although, some cotton fabrics may be specially treated to make them moisture wicking.

It has been revealed that double checking the tags on your tops, or reading about the materials it's made of will help you pick proper shirts for your workouts. And thankfully, you can find moisture-wicking materials in tanks, short sleeve tees, long sleeve tees and hoodies.

In a recent development, so, why buy a workout shirt anyway? We've all worked out out in a regular cotton t-shirt at one time or another, and while it certainly won't ruin your gym session, it won't make it more enjoyable either.

The result of wearing shirts designed for athletic performance is that the fabric from which they're made feels drier and cooler against the skin.

Industry observers note that "Moisture-wicking [shirts] can be especially beneficial when the body is subject to higher temperatures, like during a workout or a hot summer day," Dr. Hartman explains. Plus, keeping things cool and dry under your shirt can actually minimize a slew of complications.

It has been revealed that "Buildup of sweat can lead to irritation which can appear as red, flaky patches or breakouts, which appear as red papules or pustules that may involve the hair follicle," explains Dr. Garshick.

According to recent reports, there are some body odor perks, too (or lack thereof), according to Dr. Hartman. "Body odor occurs when sweat mixes with natural bacteria found on the skin. The less sweat on the skin, the less body odor.".

The listing comes as Anthropic, the tech giant behind the popular AI chatbot Claude, officially made its much-anticipated stock market debut on Thursday, Nov. 19, with its shares seeing massive volatility.

It's crucial to mention that ANT isn't a cryptocurrency but a traditional stock. Coinbase's support for ANT shares highlights the company's efforts to expand its offerings beyond crypto into traditional financial markets.

Sources indicate that anthropic has set a fresh historic precedent, having successfully raised about $81 billion in its initial public offering (IPO). This is the biggest IPO ever.

But as Anthropic shares started trading on the Nasdaq exchange, the ANT ticker saw massive volatility.

At the initial peak, Anthropic's market cap exceeded $2 trillion, surpassing SpaceX's valuation when it debuted on the market in June.

Anthropic shares slipped to around $95 as the stock gave back a significant chunk of its gains. This was partly due to investors looking to book their profits.

Nonetheless, Anthropic shares were still trading comfortably above their $83 IPO price.

The volatility surrounding Anthropic's stock market debut signals increasing doubts about the AI investment craze.

The listing of Anthropic shares is just one of Coinbase's moves to enter traditional financial markets.

Instead of just providing cryptocurrency trading, the exchange is looking to become a platform for multiple asset classes.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, Coinbase had already listed Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual futures for eligible non-U.S. owners on Nov. 18.

The perpetual futures were derivative contracts that allowed traders to speculate on Anthropic's valuation before its shares officially started trading on Nasdaq.

Sources indicate that with the latest listing, eligible Coinbase people in the U.S. and U.K. can now trade the publicly listed Anthropic shares.

Anthropic's blockbuster debut comes as financial markets have been rocked by recent volatility, with tech stocks and crypto facing selling pressure.

#87840. Ice Dives Are the Simple Therapy Trick that Rewired My Anxious Brain

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1892 w)

Ice Dives Are the Simple Therapy Trick that Rewired My Anxious Brain

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A few weeks ago, I was more anxious than I had been in a long time—or maybe ever.
  • While calling your sister is always a good idea, mine also happens to be a clinical fellow at McLean Hospital, a.k.a.
  • Industry observers note that “I’m not hanging up until you do it,” she remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A few weeks ago, I was more anxious than I had been in a long time—or maybe ever. My thoughts were racing, and even for someone who deals with her share of anxiety, I was way beyond my normal self. So, I did what any person would do in that moment: I called my sister.

While calling your sister is always a good idea, mine also happens to be a clinical fellow at McLean Hospital, a.k.a. one of the leading psychiatric institutions in the whole country, so let’s just say she knows how to handle an anxious person. Her suggestion was to go to the kitchen, grab a big bowl, fill it with ice water, and then dunk my face in it. I wasn’t exactly thrilled by the idea. It seemed like a whole bunch of work for something that couldn’t possibly help me in such a state.

Industry observers note that “I’m not hanging up until you do it,” she remarked. She could tell I thought the idea was silly, and that I was probably going to skip it. And, I did think it was silly, but she seemed weirdly passionate that I submerge my face into a bowl of freezing water, so I complied. I grabbed a bowl, filled it with water and ice cubes, and reluctantly got my face wet, just barely making sure my nose and eyes were underwater.

According to recent reports, I felt better basically instantly. The racing thoughts subsided and I could finally see straight. Even more impressive is the fact that once I reentered the situation that was making me anxious, all that nervous energy simply didn’t return. I was reset and relaxed. All it took was a bucket of water and about 30 seconds.

The trick—or, skill, I should say—that my sister taught me comes from dialectical behavioral therapy (DBT), a modality that was created by Marsha Linehan, PhD, who recently passed away at 83 years old. It was a breakthrough treatment for people facing extreme mental health challenges like chronic suicidality and borderline personality disorder, which Linehan revealed she struggled with in 2011, decades after DBT became the gold standard for treating those conditions.

Sources indicate that whether or not you are someone who deals with a formal mental health diagnosis or the occasional tough moment, DBT skills can make a major difference. The cold water trick my sister taught me is called an “ice dive,” and it’s one of four simple DBT tools that can help snap you out of a range of intense emotions quickly. Now, any time I feel myself getting heightened, my immediate next thought is: I should go grab a bucket of ice water. Call me converted.

Here’s how you can practice this skill too, plus, the three others that work just as well—and don’t involve water.

It has been revealed that meet the experts: Shireen Rizvi, PhD, is a clinical psychologist and director of psychology training and DBT services and research at Montefiore Einstein in Latest York City. Vibh Forsythe Cox, PhD, is a clinical associate professor at the University of Washington and the director of the Marsha M. Linehan DBT clinic.

At this point, you’ve pretty much gotten the entire gist of an ice dive, but let’s recap: All it takes is a bowl significant enough to get your full face in and some chilly water. (The colder the better, but it doesn’t need to reach ice bath territory.) Once you’ve got that, place it on a low-set table or even on the ground—you want to be bending over when you dunk your head in to mimic something closer to a dive—take a deep breath, and submerge your face, especially around your nasal passages and eyes, for as long as possible. 30 seconds is ideal, but that may feel like a really long time at first. Just go for as long as you can, and feel free to repeat multiple times for a cumulative total of 30 seconds.

Industry observers note that as for what is going on when you do this: Dunking your face in cold water triggers what is called the mammalian dive reflex, indicates Shireen Rizvi, PhD, a clinical psychologist and director of psychology training and DBT services and research at Montefiore Einstein in New York City. “It’s automatic,” she says. “You’re not doing anything consciously to create the reaction, which is there to help mammals survive cold water.”.

In a recent development, an ice dive triggers a survival mode where our bodies reduce our heart rate, slow down our breathing, and redirect blood to our vital organs, she explains. Under water, it helps you stay alive, but on land, it helps calm just about any activating emotion you might be experiencing. And, your face being what’s submerged is critical to get this specific reaction; getting in an ice bath where your face isn’t underwater actually spikes your heart rate due to cold shock, for example.

Recent findings suggest that basically, an ice dive forces your body to focus on the bare necessities, like staying calm. It’s best used anytime your emotions are reaching a 90-plus on a scale of 1 to 100, Rizvi claims, whether the emotion is anxiety, anger, stress, jealousy, or anything else. If you’re feeling it intensely and your heart rate is up, an ice dive can help.

There’s one other handy use case too: If you’re ruminating. “When your body is in a survival mode, it's pulling resources back, and it actually also pulls your attention too, so if you have a lot of thoughts floating around in your head making you anxious, this can also help clear your mind temporarily,” notes Vibh Forsythe Cox, PhD, a clinical associate professor at the University of Washington and the director of the Marsha M. Linehan DBT clinic. Think of it this way: “You can't be thinking about a grocery list if you have just fallen into ice water,” she says.

And, while this trick has completely changed the game for me, I have some good news: There are three others that all have the same effect sans H2O.

In a recent development, an ice dive makes up the very first letter—T for temperature—in the TIPP acronym, which is a part of DBT’s distress tolerance pillar. The rest (intense exercise, paced breathing, and paired muscle relaxation) can all swiftly calm and reset your nervous system, no liquid necessary.

All four skills have a similar basic mechanism. They take you from a heightened state (or a distressed one, to use DBT-speak) where your sympathetic nervous system is activated and bring you back into a relaxed one, where your parasympathetic nervous system is in the driver’s seat again. They’re not about talking or reflecting; they’re about helping you feel better in a moment when emotions are extreme.

In a recent development, “These are skills that act to regulate your physiology,” Cox states. “Oftentimes when you are having an intense emotion, you think you have to handle it with your mind. These are skills that help you handle it with your body.” Of course, once you’re out of that intense moment, you may want to call on other mental tools and process what happened—but that’s not where you’re at when you’re calling on a TIPP skill. They’re for when you’re in crisis mode.

You can use any of them at any time with one important caveat: All TIPP skills are meant to rapidly slow down your heart rate, so if you’re someone with a heart condition or who takes meds like beta blockers, talk to your doctor first before trying any of them, Rizvi indicates.

Without further ado, here’s what you need to know about the other three skills.

The I in TIPP stands for intense exercise. This may sound similarly prohibitive to needing a bowl of water, but it’s actually quite simple. All you really need to do is get moving for about 30 seconds. Do some all-out jumping jacks, pump your arms up and down as fast as you can while sitting in your chair, or get into a plank. Just get your heart rate up and your muscles feel fatigued. “It feels paradoxical, but when you end that short burst of exercise, everything slows down,” Rizvi states.

Recent findings suggest that there’s also an added benefit to going with exercise. When you’re feeling a heightened emotion, one of the ways your sympathetic nervous system reacts is by sending out glucose into your bloodstream, Cox says. Again, this is an automatic, physical reaction, and it’s what gives you the energy for either a fight or flight response. But since you're probably not feeling anxious or angry because you need to escape a pack of hungry wolves, you probably won’t end up literally running away or fighting them off and using that energy. Exercising eats up some of that extra glucose, helping you get back to baseline.

If you’ve ever done box breathing, you’ve done the first P in TIPP. All it involves is breathing in and out in a controlled manner for a set number of seconds each time. “The main core of this technique is that your out breath needs to be longer than your in breath,” notes Cox. “That is what activates your parasympathetic nervous system and slows everything down.”.

In addition to keeping your out breath longer than your in breath (say four seconds in and eight out), you also want to make sure you’re breathing from your diaphragm, Rizvi says. You can monitor this by placing your hand on your belly. If it’s rising and falling with each breath, you’re breathing from your diaphragm.

If you’re looking for an entry-level DBT skill, or one that you can do in pretty much any context, this is a good one to master. “I find paced breathing in particular is something that you can usually do no matter where you are or what you're doing,” Rizvi says. It takes no setup, no resources, and you can even do it in plain sight without people noticing.

It has been revealed that finally, the last TIPP skill is paired muscle relaxation. “When we are having an intense emotion, our body tenses up,” Cox indicates. “This helps release some of that tension.”.

Sources indicate that to do this skill, start at one end of your body and systematically work your way up or down, tensing and releasing your muscles throughout and saying the word “relax” each time. Pairing the muscle tensing with the word relax also helps train them—and therefore you—to relax on command, Cox says.

There are plenty of guided paired muscle relaxation routines you can follow online, but you can also just do it on your own, tensing as many muscle groups as you’d like (or have time for).

Don’t have time to reread an article in a moment of crisis? Here are the quick and simple basics of all the TIPP skills for when you need to use them ASAP.

Industry observers note that no matter which one you go for, remember this: “Emotions fire in the order of milliseconds,” Cox claims. That means that no matter how intense the thing you’re feeling is, it will pass, and probably much faster than you think. Sometimes, all our brains need is a reset initiated by our bodies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that italy’s largest banking group, Intesa Sanpaolo, increased its spot altcoin ETF holdings according to a newly introduced disclosure. This follows capital rotation out of Bitcoin products by a slew of traditional firms amid dwindling market sentiment.

It has been revealed that the bank’s disclosed crypto ETF holdings grew in Q3 2026 to $108.56 million, up $17 million, while digital asset prices moved sideways. In June, total assets were worth $90 million as it looked to diversify and grow holdings systematically.

According to recent reports, bitcoin, the largest asset in the portfolio, was reduced to make room for altcoins in a possible bid to diversify assets. At the end of Q2, BTC holdings stood at $69.32 million but dropped slightly to above $61 million last quarter. The firm’s Ethereum exposure also dropped to $5 million.

However, Solana and XRP products filled the vacuum, highlighting institutional appetite for these assets. At the time of writing, the bank’s spot Solana ETF exposure is at $14.1 million after its investment in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF ballooned from seven shares to 875,407 shares.

Intesa’s XRP investment also grew over the same period to $27.2 million, driven mainly by 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF. The firm’s shares in the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF remained unchanged across both quarters.

More broadly, the bank reduced its Bitcoin ETF exposure and increased SOL and XRP products. Most experts believe it follows the current market trend, and firms, especially traditional companies, need to diversify to make up for Bitcoin’s decline.

Recent findings suggest that historically, during bear phases, there’s a huge rotation of capital into altcoins, though it’s not sustained for long. As expected, Solana and XRP become institutional favorites, while Ethereum trades similarly to Bitcoin.

The former have the potential to record spikes within the red wave, like in 2022 before the approval of spot ETF products in the United States. These products opened up digital assets to a new stash of traditional capital.

Sources indicate that intesa and other banks have since increased their crypto exposure, driven by the need to diversify assets and a broader adoption spree. Heightened institutional and retail interests pushed Bitcoin to an all-time high above $125k last year. Right now, BTC trades at $63,819, while Ethereum is slightly below $1,800.

  • After introducing the latest and improved bZ (formerly the bZ4X) in late 2025, the electric SUV swiftly became one of the most popular EVs in the US.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that toyota now offers three fully electric SUVs: the bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland. Here’s how they stack up.

After introducing the latest and improved bZ (formerly the bZ4X) in late 2025, the electric SUV swiftly became one of the most popular EVs in the US.

In the first nine months of 2026, it was the fourth-best-selling electric vehicle, behind the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.

With two additional electric SUVs now on sale, the CH-R and bZ Woodland, Toyota has suddenly become one of America’s top-selling EV brands.

Its EV sales have nearly tripled this year. According to Cox Automotive, Toyota ranked as the third most popular EV brand behind Tesla and Rivian in the third quarter.

Toyota offers three distinct electric vehicles: the 2027 bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland, each designed for different lifestyles, so which one is the best fit for you?

Industry observers note that after launching the updated model last year, the 2027 bZ starts at $34,980. With the $1,595 delivery fee, the starting price is $36,576.

It has been revealed that that’s for the standard 2027 Toyota bZ XLE FWD with an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 236 miles. For longer range, you can upgrade to the FWD Plus model, which offers up to 314 miles and starts at $37,980 (excluding the delivery fee).

The Toyota bZ is available in XLE and Limited grades, with front- or all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrains.

Two battery options are offered: The 57.7 kWh battery on the standard XLE FWD provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 236 miles, while the larger 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 288 miles of range on the XLE AWD and 314 miles on the XLE FWD Plus model.

FWD models produce either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models deliver a combined 338 hp.

Sources indicate that the 2027 bZ also has a built-in NACS port, so you can use Tesla Superchargers without needing a separate adapter. Toyota noted it takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

It has been revealed that inside, the 2027 bZ features Toyota’s updated cabin design. The setup features a 7″ LCD customizable Multi Information Display (MID) and a new 14″ Toyota Audio Multimedia display screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The bZ is essentially designed as an everyday driver with a long driving range, modern tech, and available AWD.

Industry observers note that for those looking for a bigger, more rugged option, the 2027 bZ Woodland may be a better fit. The Woodland is 6″ longer than the standard bZ and comes with standard AWD.

The longer body opens up more interior space, with up to 74.3 cubic feet of storage compared to the bZ with up to 67.1 cubic feet.

Unlike the bZ, the Woodland model has a standard AWD powertrain with Toyota’s X-Mode control system.

The setup delivers a combined 375 horsepower, 37 hp more than the standard bZ, making it Toyota’s most powerful EV at the moment.

It also adopts a more commanding, upright stance with 8.3″ of ground clearance and 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Although it uses the same 74.7 kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland’s EPA-estimated range drops to 281 miles because of the added weight and power. Upgrading to the optional all-terrain tires sacrifices even more range, with up to 260 miles.

Sources indicate that like the bZ, the Woodland also has a built- in NACS port. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes around 30 minutes.

Inside, the bZ Woodland features the same 7″ LCD customizable Multi Information Display (MID) and 14″ Toyota Audio Multimedia display screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380. All variants include standard roof rails, Dual Qi-capable wireless device chargers, heated front seats and steering wheel, and Digital Key capabilities.

Last, but not least, the C-HR is a smaller, sporty, coupe-like electric SUV. The 2027 Toyota C-HR starts at $37,080, or $2,100 more than the standard bZ.

Sources indicate that it’s about 6.7″ shorter than the bZ, with a smaller wheelbase, but also comes with standard AWD. The dual-motor AWD setup delivers a combined 338 hp, not quite as much as the bigger, more powerful Woodland.

The C-HR is available exclusively with the 74.7 kWh battery, which provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 287 miles for the SE grade with 18″ wheels.

Upgrading to 20″ wheels adds a street-ready look but offers slightly less EPA range, with up to 273 miles.

The coupe-like design adds a sleek look and opens up interior space, with up to 59.5 cubic feet of rear cargo space when the rear seats are folded. That’s slightly more than the bZ, which offers up to 56.9 cubic feet.

Inside, the C-HR features the same setup as its other EVs, including a 7″ slim driver’s display and 14″ central infotainment screen.

Like Toyota’s other electric SUVs, the C-HR has a native NACS port. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes about 30 minutes.

Sources indicate that these are all basically the same small vehicles. I did not fit in any of them (6’ 2”) it is so frustrating to have less than 300 miles of range on AWD versions that are supposed to be better models.

It is 2026 over a decade since EVs arrived and over 5 years after the Tesla Model Y with practically zero competition almost at same price (Rivian R2 may be next year when affordable versions ship.) BMW, Mercedes and Volvo need $10k more. Hyundai has kept EV5 out of USA.

It is almost like none of the Legacy automakers want any SUV that can compete on price.

The 2027 Toyota C-HR EV is available in two trims: SE and XSE. Standard features include two wireless Qi phone chargers, low-profile roof rails, Fabric/SofTex-trimmed seating, heated front seats and steering wheel, Toyota Safety Sense 3.0, and a power liftgate.

Which Toyota electric SUV would you choose? The bZ, C-HR, or bZ Woodland? Or would you choose another EV? Let us know your pick in the comments. Next year, Toyota will add the Highland EV, its first three-row electric SUV.

Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, its fourth frontier model release in three weeks, and on the eve of the heavily anticipated Anthropic IPO.

This isn’t just a normal model release. For one, it’s incredibly good. Neon posts 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against 59 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 57 for GPT-6.2 Sol. It takes the Vals Index at 70.9%, AutomationBench at 56.3% against Opus 5.5’s 42.5%, and GraphWalks long-context retrieval at 95.2% against Opus 5.5’s 66.8%.

Sources indicate that beyond just the outperformance, Google has been releasing at a pace nobody else is matching. It dropped Argon in mid-October. Carbon on October 28. Hydrogen last week. Google owns its silicon, its data centers, and its distribution, and it is using all three to iterate faster than labs that rent compute. And it has some speculating that Google has already achieved RSI (recursive self-improvement), the final step ahead of super intelligence.

Industry observers note that so Google has caught up at the top of the AI race. Just in time for the ANT IPO.

Anthropic will be priced at $83, 6.4% above the top of its $70 to $78 range, valuing the company around $1.5 trillion fully diluted. On the 825 million shares in the original terms, that’s roughly $68.5 billion raised, and about $94.5 billion counting the separate $26 billion private placement from its compute suppliers. It trades Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT. Notably, ANT has been trading on Hyperliquid in the $90-$100 range for the past week but popped to $105 this morning.

The valuation math is a 55% step-up from the $965 billion May round and about 25% below the $2 trillion Anthropic was reportedly chasing in September. Revenue ran $33.2 billion through nine months against $2.5 billion a year earlier, a 13x increase. Annualize that and $1.5 trillion is roughly 34 times sales.

Sources indicate that that’s a steep raise given the macro backdrop and the Fed calling for more hikes for longer. AI stocks have been shaky over the past month and even moreso since Jensen Huang left Nvidia. Not the most confident market headed into the 2nd $1T+ IPO of the year.

In a recent development, so what does it mean for today’s price action? Personally, I expect a pop to the $95-$105 level that Hyperliquid has been pricing out for weeks, and it likely sees a spike higher. But there will be massive volatility, and it’s very likely to trade under that $83 level over the coming days and weeks. Especially given the new (surprise) headwinds from Google with its outperforming model.

It has been revealed that we will find out soon enough. Good luck to everyone trading it today.

  • To find the GOATs, our fashion team and I tested more than 50 styles—everything from V-neck tees and tank tops to classic white crewnecks—wearing them under button-downs, sweaters, and even on their own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A GREAT UNDERSHIRT is my first line of defense against sweat, stains, and overheating. It’s like the menswear equivalent of SPF. I learned that the hard way years ago, when I wore a flimsy cotton tee under a light-blue dress shirt to a summer wedding and, by cocktail hour, looked like I’d run a 10K instead of walked down the aisle. Never again. Now, if I’m layering under a dress shirt or sweater, I want something that works hard without me ever thinking about it. The best undershirts are so comfortable, I forget they’re even on. Unlike cheap, bulky options that ride up, trap heat, or lose their shape after a few washes, the real standouts are lightweight, moisture-wicking, and cut with a trim fit that stays put without squeezing the life out of you. They also tuck away neatly into trousers and save your other shirts from pit stains.

To find the GOATs, our fashion team and I tested more than 50 styles—everything from V-neck tees and tank tops to classic white crewnecks—wearing them under button-downs, sweaters, and even on their own. The winners disappear under your clothes like a good stunt double, regulate temperature like built-in AC, and keep you looking cool, calm, and collected from your morning commute to last call.

Sources indicate that hanes is perhaps the most famous undershirt brand on the planet. I’ve been wearing its undergarments since I was about 10 years old, and over the time, they've just become better in terms of fit and feel. For example, I’ve been wearing Hanes’ performance undershirt for four months, and it’s consistently comfortable, breathable, and snug in all the right places.

Recent findings suggest that the shoulders sit perfectly without pulling, the chest drapes close without clinging, and the sleeves are tailored to follow your arms without cutting into your biceps. When an undershirt feels this light, I brace myself for it to be flimsy and tear like tissue, but it's impressively solid—and I didn’t even sweat in it. Unlike other undershirts that I’ve tested, this one has a structured collar and hem that keeps its shape. The polyester-rayon fabric is extra smooth and cool to the touch, even after wearing it for hours at the office. I also appreciate that the fabric blend is much lighter in weight than a traditional cotton undershirt.

After putting it through at least eight washes, I noticed that the fabric didn’t fade or shrink. One way I preserve it is by letting it air dry instead of tossing it in the dryer under high heat. It’s long enough to tuck in and doesn’t bunch under an overshirt. Since it's blended with a hint of stretch, I could grab a box off a high shelf without any restriction. Hanes uses the same double-needle stitching to reinforce the neck, sleeves, and hem as with their regular undershirts. This will stand up to years of washing and wearing with steady use. It only comes in white, but you can wear it with so many different fits—solo or layered.

Read More: Best T-Shirts for Men.

Sources indicate that mack Weldon was founded to reinvent men's underwear and loungewear with better fabric blends and quality construction. Take its V-neck style undershirt that I've been wearing for a couple months now. It’s cut from a polyamide-elastane blend—the same kind of technical fabric in our favorite workout clothes. It’s got that silky-soft hand feel with real stretch baked in. I can lift my arms, reach overhead, and wrestle into a jacket on the subway, and I don’t feel any tugging in the arms. The neckline sits low enough to disappear when I don’t want it to be seen under my dress shirts, but not so deep it feels flimsy or overly delicate.

Recent findings suggest that what really sold me, though, is the breathability. Even under my chunky sweaters with some heft, I never break a sweat or find myself needing to flap my knit like I'm trying to cool off. Since it has a slim fit, it sits close to my skin without being tight, but stays dry when I’m making my way through the muggy subway or sitting in non-air-conditioned areas at the office. I tossed it in the wash at least six times and the white still looks just as good as the day it came out the pack.

According to recent reports, tommy John V-neck undershirt is step above your average option when it comes to polished layering. Its slim cut and modal fabric give it shape and structure, so it skims the body without feeling tight—perfect for showing off a chest workout without clinging in an unflattering way.

One of the best features is how it tucks. The snug-but-not-tight fit keeps the shirt neatly in place under dress shirts or sweaters, so you don’t get bunching or riding up. This makes it ideal for formal and office-ready attire, where a clean, smooth base layer is essential. It’s also stretchy without being too thin and has yet to pill, five washes later. I recommend letting it air dry, so it doesn’t shrink or become tight since the undershirt has a slim fit.

Industry observers note that after multiple wears, the V collar doesn’t give “bacon neck”, which makes it look worn-out. It sits closer to the neck than Mack Weldon’s version, but I still can hide it by closing the top two buttons of my dress shirt. I love the buttery-soft feel, which is breathable and light even in warmer 70-degree temps.

A major qualm with undershirts is their neckline can easily get ratted through the wash. We found Jockey's Made in America tees to keep a strong neckline and provide overall durability as an everyday undershirt. This is one of those cases where it's worth paying the extra bucks for an American-made garment.

In a recent development, the Made in America factor isn't just for show. The quality that comes with it is apparent. The construction is clean and the fabric is thick enough that this undershirt can double as a plain white tee. So if you ever need to shed a layer or two, you can fall back on this as a base layer t-shirt. You can even style it on a hot day with just a pair of shorts.

More importantly, we found that Jockey has nailed the standard 100% cotton plain white undershirt in the best way possible. It feels like a traditional soft cotton tee, but after putting it through the wash and dry cycles more than a dozen times, it managed to withstand all the wear and tear and stay intact, proving its durability. The fabric even has a tech built-in to reduce piling and fading. And I love that the cotton is engineered to be able to wick away sweat in a heartbeat to keep me fresh all day. The only thing is that the fabric isn't wrinkle-resistant, so store these shirts carefully.

ATEK’s Stay Cooling undershirt is engineered for guys who run hot. The nylon-spandex blend feels slick and technical—almost like performance base-layer gear—but that’s exactly why it works. It wicks sweat fast, dries quickly, and stays smooth under slimmer dress shirts without bunching or clinging. I’ve been wearing it while commuting and traveling since 2021, especially on days when I’m bouncing between the subway, the office, and post-work plans. The stretch makes it easy to move in, and after dozens of washes, it hasn’t shrunk or warped.

In a recent development, gollayan put it through even tougher paces. He wore it under tailored dress shirts during long shoot days and under knit polos in the summer heat, noting that it kept sweat marks at bay and didn’t show through lightweight fabrics. He also flagged how well it holds its shape through the torso—no bacon-neck collar, no sagging by 4 p.m. If you love the soft, matte hand-feel of classic cotton, this one may feel a bit slick and synthetic. But that’s the trade-off for serious cooling power.

There has never been another brand with more hype around it than the early 1990s "My Calvins" undergarment campaign. But Calvin Klein's classic ribbed tank is not just hype, it is actually a really solid undershirt. If you prefer the minimal fabric feel of a tank or you just wear them when it's hot out then Calvins are hard to beat. And these, as undershirts, are practically perfect in terms of fabric, fit, and durability.

The full cotton fabric is stretchy despite having no built-in elastane or spandex. We love its soft-to-touch quality as well as natural breathability, the latter helps with wicking away sweat. The classic fit we found is slim without being constricting and they're just long enough to be tucked in if you need to but they can hang out without showing. The classic scoop neckline and seaming have also lasted well, and the fabric, even after over a dozen wash and dry cycles, has remained as stretchy, soft, and breezy.

For layering, we love putting it underneath a button-down or sweater/sweatshirt, though if you’re prone to underarm, we’d advise against this undershirt as your go-to.

According to recent reports, bugatchi’s crew neck tee is another great option that blurs the line between undershirt and standalone tee, but it leans more dressy than most. Made from a silky-soft Pima cotton, it has a luxe feel and fluid drape that’s more cocktail hour than couch rotting. I’ve worn it tucked into slacks with dress shoes for a fancy dinner, and it held its own. The fabric skims the body without clinging, and the finish reads sleek, not sporty.

It doesn’t have a durable ribbed collar like other dressier T-shirts, but it has a clean binding, which keeps its shape and frames the neck well. Compared to Reigning Champ’s athletic cut, this tee offers a touch more room in the torso, which flatters buffer guys. It layers neatly under jackets, but isn’t skin-tight. Out of all the undershirts on this list, this one has the best color options. When I'm heading into the city for dinner, I go with the mint to pair with cream dress pants for a clean, sharp ensemble. But for weekend errands or a coffee run, I throw on the air blue with jeans.

Gap has long been my go-to for affordable basics that punch above their price point. This undershirt is no different. While it’s not the trendiest or most technical, the shirt is made with an ultra-light, superfine jersey that’s buttery smooth, breathable, and almost weightless. It feels so nice and comfy that I lounge and sleep in it too. Unlike your average undershirt, which can feel a little thick or rough over time, this one stays silky and cool after multiple wears, making it perfect for layering under a blazer or shacket. Or, you could just throw it on to kick back on the couch.

It has been revealed that the straight fit is a major win for guys who want an undershirt that feels natural rather than overly snug or restrictive. The looser cut drapes smoothly over the body without awkward bunching, so you can wear it all day. In terms of the quality after washing, I have never seen the fabric pill. This kind of cotton manages to stay incredibly soft, cycle after cycle, speaking to its high quality.

It has been revealed that at first glance, Reigning Champ’s jersey slim T-shirt might look like your everyday summer tee, but don’t be fooled. Yes, it has that easy, breezy fabric you want in a lightweight layer, but it’s not filmy, too thin, or see-through. It’s made from premium cotton that’s both smooth and breathable, yet structured enough that it retains its shape. I've tossed it in the wash at least four times now, and it still comes out looking good as new. The cut is slim and subtly tapered at the hem, which looks sharp on athletic builds and lean frames.

Unlike looser, floppier collars that stretch out after a few cycles, this one is topped with a rib-bound collar that stays in place. It’s one of the only lightweight undershirts we tested where the collar didn’t droop, curl, or widen after wash two. I’ve worn it solo with shorts and jeans for coffee runs and quick errands. It also handled light activity in the park without showing any sweat and still looked fresh after hours of wear. Bonus: The color selection offers a number of neutrals that work for every outfit.

If you’re looking for the most breathable undershirt, it’s hard to beat the Uniqlo AIRism T-shirt. It’s made from a lightweight, high-tech fabric that consists of a polyester-elastane blend that dries rapidly and helps regulate body temperature to keep you cool and comfy all day. I wore the tee during a full-day shoot under a denim overshirt and didn’t overheat once even under direct sun and studio lights.

It wicked away sweat faster than I expected and, more impressively, dried completely by the time I was back indoors. I also put it through a few airport and train travel days and the stretch fit held its shape, didn’t smell funky, and kept me feeling way fresher than any basic cotton tee could. Whether you’re layering it under a button-down or wearing it solo on a hot commute, it keeps you cool, not clammy, even in peak humidity.

Industry observers note that the ribbed texture is what really sets this tee apart from your average undershirt. It adds natural stretch and recovery, which means the shirt contours to your body, especially around the chest, arms and torso, without feeling tight or restrictive. The result? A more sculpted, flattering fit that holds its shape throughout the day. I tested it on a few hours-long photoshoots and can confirm: it doesn’t ride up, it breathes well, and the collar doesn’t sag by mid-afternoon.

The fabric itself, a soft organic and recycled cotton-blend jersey, has just the right amount of weight. The fine ribbing, which creates raised vertical lines that look like subtle ridges, adds structure without veering into ’90s tank top territory, and the slim fit gives it that clean, tailored base layer vibe. It’s also a subtle style flex: If you shed your overshirt, this undershirt doesn’t look like a throwaway white tee. It actually holds its own, especially when paired with jeans or trousers.

If you’re looking for a classic cotton undershirt that feels premium but not flashy, Brooks Brothers’ Supima Cotton V-Neck is it. It’s not built for performance like Mack Weldon’s tech-forward v-neck; it leans hard into comfort and breathability. Produced from Supima cotton, it’s noticeably smoother, softer, and more durable than other cotton shirts. It doesn’t hug the body as tightly, which actually makes it more forgiving on paunchier guts and more comfortable for long days on the move. This is the undershirt for guys who want something that disappears under button-ups; more work meeting than gym locker room.

The v-neck stayed completely hidden, even with the top two buttons undone, and the fit was trim enough that it didn’t bunch or add bulk under the shirt. Even under hot studio lights, I didn’t feel like I was sweating bullets. After three washes at home (cold wash, low tumble dry), the softness held up. It stayed smooth against the skin, with no pilling, collar warping or shrinkage. The seams stayed flat and clean, and the fabric has just enough weight to feel substantial, but still light enough to hide under thinner shirting.

According to recent reports, of all the undershirts we’ve tested, Fruit of the Loom’s 8-Pack easily provides the most value per wear. While it’s not as soft or moisture-wicking as more expensive shirts we’ve tried, it has a polyester-cotton blend that’s still comfortable and breathable enough to get you through the day. It has been revealed that the Skims Classic T-shirt is a jack of all trades because it works as a base layer, a solo tee, or even a sleep shirt—it’s that comfortable. Recent findings suggest that the key to the 72-Hour Tee is its merino wool fabric. Huckberry engineered this tee to utilize the natural features of merino wool, which is breathable, moisture-wicking, odor-resistant, and temperature-regulating. The goal of the 72-Hour Tee was to create an undershirt that you can wear for three days straight without getting gross. Our testers wore it during long flights as long as 16 hours overseas. The new Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ covered 539 miles without stopping to charge, making range anxiety look like a thing of the past.

Mercedes-Benz overhauled the EQS electric sedan, including a bigger battery and an 800V electrical architecture.

The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ uses a 122 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 467 miles.

Industry observers note that while that’s already impressive, the electric sedan will likely go even farther in everyday driving conditions. During Edmunds recent EV Range Test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ drove a whopping 539 miles without stopping to charge.

The EQS beat its own EPA estimate by 72 miles and is now the longest-range electric sedan Edmunds has ever tested, beating the Lucid Air, the first EV to break the 500-mile mark. The only EV that has it beat is the Cadillac Escalade IQ, which managed 558 miles from its massive 205 kWh battery.

During the test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ was also more efficient than its official numbers suggest.

The upcoming EQS used 29.6 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 28 kWh per 100 miles. In comparison, the 2025 Mercedes EQS 450+ covered 464 miles and used 34 kWh per 100 miles during the same test, so the improvements are considerable.

Edmunds observed a peak charging rate of 350 kW, in line with Mercedes’ estimates, while it sustained an average of 222 kW throughout the session.

Both beat the older EQS, which reached a peak charge rate of 208 kW and sustained an average of 175 kW.

The new Mercedes EQS 450+ added 825 miles of range in an hour, and 100 miles in just over 7 minutes, nearly twice the speed of the 2025MY.

Industry observers note that the Edmunds EV Range Test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions. It includes 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.

How much is too much? 539 miles on a single charge is impressive, but do you need it? In a recent “nationally representative” survey, BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.

The study indicated that 73% consider 25, 50, or 75 miles enough to cover their daily driving. However, 42% said they would require at least 300 miles of range before they would consider an EV.

Industry observers note that if you have access to a home charger, nothing beats waking up with a full charge every day. Meanwhile, public charging continues to improve, giving EV drivers more reliable options on longer trips.

Faster charging also helps. Another 53% remarked they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in around 10 minutes.

Industry observers note that in the same Edmunds EV Range Test last week, the upcoming 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive drove 436 miles on a single charge, exceeding its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles. It also used 28.3 kWh per 100 miles during the test, beating its official EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles.

The new 2027 Volvo EX60 drove 352 miles while the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric covered 392 miles during the same test.

Recent findings suggest that ready for smooth, bump-free skin? Look no further than these editor-tested and expert-approved electric razors for women, below.

Recent findings suggest that if you struggle with bumps and irritation, an electric razor might be your fresh best friend. Of course, you still need to make sure you use that electric razor properly. Dermatologists say you should follow the below best practices for a smooth shave every time.

It has been revealed that make sure your skin is well hydrated before shaving because using an electric razor over dry, irritated skin can make matters worse, states dermatologist Joshua Zeichner, MD. Dr. Robinson adds that you should also use a gentle cleanser prior to shaving. And, avoid fragrance or products known to cause irritation immediately before and after shaving, she says.

And please, do so in the direction of the hair growth, says Dr. Zeichner. Repeated strokes over the same area increase the likelihood of irritation and ingrown hairs.

It has been revealed that hydration is key. "I advise patients that they do not need a dedicated post-shave or aftercare lotion—a gentle moisturizer is just fine in these areas," indicates Dr. Robinson, who likes light, fragrance-free formulas. Aside from that, Dr. Robinson recommends making sure you follow any specific instructions on the product package—in other words, you should actually read the directions.

It has been revealed that at the end of the day, everyone's going to have their personal preference, and it's not worth, ahem, splitting hairs if you prefer one type of razor over another. That being said, if your skin is prone to irritation, it might be time to ditch the traditional razor. With an electric razor, you’re not scraping against the skin really hard like a traditional razor does, claims dermatologist Cameron Rokhsar, MD. This means that you won't see a lot of the cuts and burns that sometimes result from a manual blade, says Dr. Rokhsar. There are also areas of the body that might be better suited to shave with an electric razor. "Most women's electric razors are designed for our curvy areas," says Dr. Ploch. "I prefer electric razors around the ankles because manual razors cut this area easily.".

Keeping your electric razor clean is incredibly crucial, indicates Dr. Rokhsar. Many derms will recommend changing a manual razor every time you shave, but you can't do that with an electric one, which makes running the blades under warm water after use a crucial step. This will keep it free of hair, shaving cream, and other residues.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Rokhsar also recommends swiping over the blades and the outside of the razor with a rubbing alcohol-soaked cotton ball regularly. "Especially if it sits in your bathroom moisture, bacteria will accumulate on the blades," he notes. "It's an easy entry point for bacteria to go down the hair follicle." That's a major no-no if you want to stay free of irritation or infection.

Sources indicate that our team of editors follow Dr. Rokhsar's advice and it hasn't led us astray. And despite evaluating some of these razors for close to a year, we are pleased that we haven't noticed any rusting after using the alcohol-soaked cotton ball.

Another tip is to actually read and follow the maintenance instructions of your device. (Admittedly, we threw ours away since we've been using these for several months and like to keep the limited space of our beauty closet as streamlined as possible.) You can also prioritize using devices like the Philips Series 5000 Electric Facial Hair Remover that's easy to clean, as the head can easily be removed so you can dump shaved hair and dead skin cells straight into the garbage.

According to recent reports, plugShare is giving its EV charging app a massive overhaul. Version 8.0 arrives worldwide for iPhone on November 10, with dark mode, a trip planner that reveals how far apart charging stops are, and a rebuilt Apple Watch app that can point you to a charger compatible with your EV.

Dark mode was one of the most-requested features from PlugShare users. It works across the app and follows your iPhone’s settings, so if your phone switches to dark mode at sunset, your charging map will, too.

The trip planner gets a small but handy change. Each charging stop now shows how far it is from both the start of your trip and the previous stop. So when you’re deciding whether to stretch to the next fast charger or stop sooner, the number you need is right there.

PlugShare now loads your saved locations, trips, and profile when you open the app or sign in, so those tabs are ready to tap. You can also open and zoom in on station photos right from their thumbnails. That’s handy when you’re trying to figure out what corner a charging station is in in a big parking lot. The app also adapts its layout to the iPhone Duo’s different screens and folded positions.

In a recent development, the rebuilt Watch app lists nearby charging stations with distances and directions. It uses the filters you’ve set on your iPhone, so if you’ve filtered for plugs that fit your EV, that carries over to your wrist.

Tap a station and you’ll see its PlugScore, the network that runs it, a small map, and which plugs it has, including NACS, CCS, CHAdeMO, or J1772. The list refreshes when you raise your wrist and open the app. You can also add a shortcut to a round or corner slot on your watch face.

The iPhone update is rolling out through the App Store. PlugShare says Android consumers will get dark mode and a redesign based on Google’s Material 3 in early 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than a year after its founding, truckless trucking brand Humble Robotics has secured more than $75 million after a $51 million Series A funding round that will fuel the firm’s transition from prototype to preproduction.

It has been revealed that the latest funding round for the driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform developer was led by Obvious Ventures with participation from other existing investors Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners. Humble noted it will use the funding for customer pilots, testing and validation, and early manufacturing.

In a recent development, “We’ve spent years proving that a truck can drive itself,” explains Humble Robotics founder and CEO, Eyal Cohen. “The harder question is how to make autonomy something a freight operator can depend on every day.”.

In a recent development, we originally covered the Humble Hauler back in May. You can check out the original article, below, then let us know what you think of the tech giant’s prospects in the comments.

The startup that dares to ask, “Why does the Macbook driving my freight around need a whole cab?” just showed off a fully driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform designed to handle containerized cargo more efficiently than ever.

Sources indicate that instead of looking at the tractor and asking how to make it work without a driver, Humble looked at the trailer, itself, redesigning the container chassis as a vehicle from the ground up. The end result isn’t just an autonomous solution, it’s an overall lighter platform without a cab that saves shippers the weight of a sleeper cab, a day cab, or the truck at all.

The Humble approach is mentioned to improve payload efficiency of shipping containers, and intended for dock-to-dock operation.

According to recent reports, “I have dedicated my career to building electric and autonomous vehicle technology,” explains Eyal Cohen, Humble Robotics’ founder and CEO. “For the first time, freight can be fully automated all the way to the loading dock. We are making freight sustainable, safe and efficient in a way no one thought was possible. And we’re doing it with an exceptional team of industry veterans and AV experts.”.

Emerging from stealth after a $24 million funding round, Humble claims to have completed its first Humble Hauler prototype in less than six months – and they’ll soon be ready to begin autonomous testing in pilot programs with a number of logistics partners.

The vehicle uses a combination of cameras, lidar, and radar for 360-degree awareness (unhindered by seeing around a cab), and uses vision-language-action models to help the system respond to upcoming scenarios.

According to recent reports, thanks to superior battery tech, a maturing global charging infrastructure, and a permanently damaged MidEast oil supply, there’s never been a better time to be an EV startup. Humble is hitting all the electric trailer buzzwords, too, while also touting the fact that the electric powertrain can reduce a company’s to volatile fuel prices even as it helps produce other cost benefits like lower maintenance costs.

There is a reason why the transportation industry developed separate cabs and trailers. Trailers can be loaded or unloaded for days and are much less expensive than trucks that serve both purposes in one piece. That allows the more expensive piece of the transport puzzle to be used more and allows the trailer to be loaded and unloaded while the cab is elsewhere working or in the shop. Query whether the savings they cite will surpass the costs of not having the flexibility of a cab and trailer design.

And if a robot like this can deliver on its promises without the baked-in inefficiencies of humanoids, they might be one step closer to provide that the most efficient solution to a problem is rarely a general one, and even rarer is it a solution that looks like a human.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) mentioned in a report published on Thursday.
